section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Arkansas, which state agency administers driver's licenses — the DMV or the DFA?
options: a:The Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV),b:The Department of Finance and Administration (DFA),c:The Department of Transportation (DOT),d:The Department of Public Safety (DPS)
note: Arkansas does not have a DMV — driver's licenses are issued by the Department of Finance and Administration (DFA). This is an important state-specific fact that is commonly tested because most states use the 'DMV' name.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum age to apply for a learner's permit in Arkansas?
note: Arkansas allows teens to apply for a learner's permit at age 14, making it one of the youngest permit ages in the nation. The permit requires supervised driving with a licensed adult before advancing to a restricted intermediate license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Arkansas's zero tolerance law for drivers under 21 sets the illegal BAC at:
note: Arkansas sets the underage DUI threshold at 0.02% BAC. A driver under 21 with a BAC of 0.02% or higher faces license suspension and criminal penalties. This threshold is lower than the adult standard of 0.08%.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal BAC limit for a driver age 21 or older in Arkansas?
note: Arkansas, like all U.S. states, sets the per se DUI limit at 0.08% BAC for drivers 21 and older. Commercial drivers face a stricter 0.04% limit. A BAC of 0.08% or higher is grounds for a DUI charge regardless of visible impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on an Arkansas rural highway with no posted speed limit sign. What is the default maximum speed?
options: a:45 mph,b:55 mph,c:60 mph,d:65 mph
note: The default speed limit on rural Arkansas highways without posted limits is 55 mph. On interstate highways the limit is higher — but rural two-lane roads default to 55 mph when no sign is present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Arkansas's Graduated Driver Licensing (GDL) program, how long must a learner's permit holder maintain a clean driving record before they can apply for an intermediate license?
options: a:30 days,b:3 months,c:6 months,d:1 year
note: Under Arkansas's GDL program, a teen holding a learner's permit must maintain a completely clean driving record (no traffic violations or at-fault crashes) for at least 6 months before they are eligible to upgrade to a Stage 2 Intermediate License.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are at a 4-way stop and arrive at the same time as a driver on your right. Who has the right of way?
options: a:You have the right of way because you are on the left,b:The driver on your right has the right of way,c:The driver traveling straight has the right of way,d:The driver traveling faster has the right of way
note: When two vehicles arrive at a 4-way stop simultaneously, the vehicle on the right has the right of way. This rule applies in Arkansas and across the United States — always yield to the driver on your right in a tie situation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing red traffic signal mean in Arkansas?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution,b:Stop completely, yield, then proceed when safe — same as a stop sign,c:The intersection is temporarily closed,d:Yield only to pedestrians
note: A flashing red signal must be treated as a stop sign in Arkansas. Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when the way is clear. A flashing yellow signal means caution — slow down but a full stop is not required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Arkansas law, which passengers in a vehicle must wear a seatbelt?
options: a:Only the driver,b:Driver and front-seat passengers only,c:All occupants of the vehicle,d:Only passengers under age 18
note: Arkansas requires all vehicle occupants — front and rear — to wear a seatbelt. The law is primary enforcement, meaning an officer can stop a vehicle solely for a seatbelt violation without needing any other reason.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit in a school zone in Arkansas when warning lights are flashing and children are present?
options: a:10 mph,b:15 mph,c:20 mph,d:25 mph
note: In Arkansas, the statutory school zone speed limit is 25 miles per hour when children are present or warning lights are flashing, unless a different limit is posted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Arkansas's GDL program, a driver with an intermediate license (age 16-17) is restricted to carrying how many unrelated minor passengers?
options: a:No minor passengers at all.,b:Only one unrelated minor passenger.,c:Up to three unrelated minor passengers.,d:No passengers under 21 who are not family.
note: Under Arkansas law, a driver with an intermediate license (ages 16 to 17) is restricted to carrying no more than one unrelated minor passenger (under age 18) unless accompanied by a licensed driver age 21 or older.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on an Arkansas highway and see an emergency vehicle pulled over with flashing lights. What does the Move Over law require?
options: a:Honk to alert the workers and maintain speed,b:Move over one lane if safe; if not, slow to a safe speed,c:Stop completely and wait for the emergency vehicle to move,d:Move over only for police vehicles — not tow trucks or utility vehicles
note: Arkansas's Move Over law requires drivers to move one lane away from any stopped emergency, law enforcement, or highway maintenance vehicle with flashing lights. If a lane change is not safely possible, slow to a speed safe for conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are about to enter a highway on-ramp. What should you do to merge safely?
options: a:Stop at the end of the on-ramp and wait for a gap in traffic,b:Match the speed of highway traffic and merge smoothly into an available gap,c:Force your way in by gradually moving into the lane,d:Signal and immediately enter the highway regardless of traffic speed
note: Merging onto a highway requires accelerating to match the flow of traffic in the target lane before merging. Stopping at the end of a ramp is dangerous because highway traffic does not expect a stationary vehicle; smooth speed-matching is the correct technique.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane road in Arkansas, when may you pass another vehicle using the left lane?
options: a:Anytime you think you can complete the pass quickly,b:Only when a dashed yellow center line is on your side of the road,c:Only on rural highways where the speed limit is 55 mph or higher,d:Whenever the road ahead appears clear for at least 100 feet
note: Passing is permitted only when a dashed yellow center line is on your side of the road, indicating the road ahead is clear enough to pass. A solid yellow line on your side prohibits crossing the center line to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit on urban streets in Arkansas when no speed limit sign is posted?
options: a:25 mph,b:30 mph,c:35 mph,d:40 mph
note: Arkansas sets the default urban speed limit at 30 mph when no other limit is posted. This applies to city streets and business districts. Residential neighborhood streets may be posted lower — always check for posted signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Arkansas, what is the minimum distance you must signal before turning or changing lanes?
options: a:50 feet,b:100 feet,c:200 feet,d:300 feet
note: Arkansas law requires drivers to signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes. Signaling well in advance gives other drivers time to react and reduces the risk of rear-end or side-swipe collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving in heavy rain on an Arkansas highway and your vehicle starts to hydroplane. What should you do?
options: a:Brake hard to regain tire contact with the road,b:Accelerate to power through the water,c:Ease off the gas and hold the steering wheel steady until tires regain traction,d:Turn the steering wheel sharply to redirect the vehicle
note: When hydroplaning, ease off the accelerator and hold the wheel steady — do not brake hard or turn sharply, as these actions can cause loss of control. The tires will regain contact once speed decreases. Driving at a lower speed in heavy rain prevents most hydroplaning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Arkansas's GDL program, intermediate license holders (age 16-17) are prohibited from operating a vehicle between which hours?
options: a:10:00 PM and 5:00 AM,b:11:00 PM and 4:00 AM,c:Midnight and 6:00 AM,d:Midnight and 5:00 AM
note: Under Arkansas GDL restrictions, drivers with an intermediate license (ages 16 to 17) cannot operate a vehicle between 11:00 PM and 4:00 AM, unless accompanied by a licensed driver age 21 or older, or traveling to/from work, school, or church activities.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Arkansas implied consent law, a driver suspected of DUI who refuses a chemical test will:
options: a:Face no penalty — refusal is a constitutional right,b:Have their license suspended for 6 months on first refusal,c:Only be penalized if convicted of DUI,d:Receive only a small fine
note: Arkansas's implied consent law means that by driving on public roads, you have consented to chemical testing. A first-offense refusal results in a 6-month license suspension that is separate from any DUI conviction. The refusal may also be used as evidence against you in court.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving in Arkansas and see a solid white line on the right edge of the road. What does it indicate?
options: a:The right edge of the travel lane — do not cross except to turn or park,b:A bike lane you may use if no cyclists are present,c:The boundary of a construction zone,d:A no-parking zone
note: A solid white line marks the right edge of the travel lane. You should not cross it except when turning, parking, or in an emergency. Edge lines help drivers stay in their lane in poor visibility conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do before backing out of a parking space in a crowded parking lot?
options: a:Honk twice and begin backing,b:Check mirrors, turn to look behind you, back slowly while watching all directions,c:Back quickly to minimize time in the travel lane,d:Signal and rely entirely on mirrors
note: Before and while backing, Arkansas drivers should check all mirrors and physically turn to look through the rear window. Back slowly while continuously checking all directions — parking lots have pedestrians, shopping carts, and other vehicles that mirrors alone may not reveal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no active warning signals (such as lights or gates), what is a driver required to do?
options: a:Always come to a complete stop before crossing.,b:Slow down, look, and listen, and stop only if a train is approaching.,c:Proceed at normal speed without checking.
note: At passive railroad crossings (which have crossbucks but no flashing lights or gates), you should slow down, look, and listen in both directions. You are only required to stop if a train is approaching or a signal is active.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the recommended following distance under normal driving conditions in Arkansas?
options: a:One second,b:Two seconds,c:Three seconds,d:Four seconds

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You see a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog at a crosswalk. What must you do in Arkansas?
options: a:Slow to 10 mph and pass carefully,b:Yield the right of way completely and stop until the pedestrian has crossed,c:Honk to alert the pedestrian you are there, then proceed,d:Yield only if the pedestrian is in your direct lane
note: Arkansas law requires drivers to yield completely to any pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog — these individuals are visually impaired. Come to a full stop and do not proceed until the pedestrian has safely cleared the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the penalty for a first-time DUI conviction in Arkansas for an adult driver?
options: a:A written warning with no license action,b:License suspension, fines, and possible jail time,c:A fine only — no license penalty on the first offense,d:Community service only
note: A first DUI conviction in Arkansas results in license suspension of 6 months, fines up to $1,000, and possible jail time of 24 hours to 1 year. The penalties increase significantly for subsequent offenses or if a minor was in the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane must you make a left turn when leaving a one-way street?
options: a:The lane nearest the left curb.,b:The lane nearest the center of the street.,c:The lane nearest the right curb.
note: On a one‑way street, all traffic moves in the same direction. For a left turn, you must start from the lane closest to the left curb so you stay in your proper lane and avoid cutting across other lanes. Then turn into the nearest legal lane on the new street.

question: What is the best action if you become tired while driving?
options: a:Open a window.,b:Stop to rest or change drivers.,c:Drink coffee.
note: If tired, stop driving and rest or switch drivers—drowsiness slows reactions and impairs judgment.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Grasp the steering wheel firmly, ease off the gas, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly to stop immediately.,c:Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, stay straight, and ease off the accelerator so the vehicle slows gradually. After the vehicle is under control and speed has dropped, apply the brakes gently and move out of the traffic lane to a safe place. Sudden braking or sharp steering can cause loss of control.

question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic, passing is:
options: a:Permitted from the left.,b:Permitted from the right.,c:Not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines between lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions mean no passing is allowed from either direction. You may cross them only when making a permitted left turn or entering/exiting a driveway or side road, when it is safe and legal.

question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of the road indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted from either direction when safe.,b:A construction zone is ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: A broken yellow center line separates traffic moving in opposite directions and indicates that passing is allowed from either direction when it can be done safely and there is no oncoming traffic. You must still judge distance and visibility carefully before passing.

question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only if the pedestrians wave to the driver.,c:Only if pedestrians obey traffic signals.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in crosswalks, whether the crosswalk is marked with lines or unmarked at an intersection. You must slow or stop if needed so pedestrians can cross safely, regardless of whether they signal or wave to you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At intersections with stop signs on all corners, who goes first?
options: a:The vehicle that arrived first at the intersection.,b:The vehicle that arrived last.,c:If two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
note: At a four-way stop, the vehicle that arrives first has the right-of-way and goes first after stopping. If two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Always move in a safe, courteous order to keep traffic flowing smoothly.

question: If you text while driving, how many times more likely are you to be in a crash than a non-distracted driver?
note: Texting while driving greatly increases your crash risk because it takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, and your attention away from driving. Studies commonly show that texting drivers are around 8–23 times more likely to crash than non-distracted drivers; many DMV manuals round this to about 10 times higher risk.

question: Why should you avoid using high beams in fog or mist?
options: a:The light will reflect back into your eyes.,b:Approaching vehicles might not see you.,c:Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.
note: In fog or mist, high beams shine into the tiny water droplets and reflect back toward your eyes, creating glare and making it harder to see. Use low beams so the light aims down at the road and improves your ability to see lane lines and the edge of the roadway.

question: If it feels like your tires have lost contact with the road (hydroplaning), you should:
options: a:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,b:Ease your foot off the gas and avoid braking.,c:Pump the brakes quickly and firmly to regain traction.
note: When you hydroplane, your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. To regain traction, gently ease your foot off the accelerator and keep the steering wheel straight. Do not brake or make sudden moves; wait until you feel the tires grip the road again before slowing more.

question: What is the typical shape and color of construction zone signs?
options: a:Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.,b:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.,c:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.
note: Construction and work zone signs are temporary warning signs. They are typically orange with black symbols or lettering and are most often diamond-shaped, though some may be rectangular for specific information like detours or lane closures.

question: You want to make a right turn, and a pedestrian with a guide dog is waiting to cross. What should you do?
options: a:Wait until the person with the guide dog has crossed before making your turn.,b:Tell the pedestrian when to cross the street.,c:Turn off your engine until they are across.
note: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes are visually impaired and always have the right-of-way. Stop and wait until they have completely crossed and are safely out of your path before making your turn. Do not give verbal instructions or pressure them to cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light is red but a police officer directs you to go through the intersection without stopping, you should:
options: a:Stop until the light turns green.,b:Follow the officer's direction and go through the intersection.,c:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.
note: A police officer’s directions override traffic signals and signs. When an officer directs you to proceed, you must follow their instructions, even if the traffic light is red, as long as you can do so safely.

question: Fatigue while driving increases the risk of what?
options: a:Falling asleep at the wheel and causing a crash.,b:Missing an exit only.,c:Being late for appointments.
note: Driving while fatigued slows your reaction time, harms your judgment, and can cause you to fall asleep at the wheel. This greatly increases the chance of a serious crash, often at high speed and without braking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you not do?
options: a:Back up on the roadway or shoulder to return to the exit.,b:Continue to the next exit and re-route.,c:Leave the freeway at the next exit and return safely.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, keep going to the next exit. Never back up on the freeway or shoulder, as traffic is moving fast and drivers do not expect a vehicle in reverse, which can easily cause a serious collision.

question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, what should you avoid?
options: a:Driving beside it for long stretches of time.,b:Following far behind to reduce wind drag.,c:Driving on its right side when on curves and hills.
note: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots along both sides, especially on the right. If you drive beside them for long stretches, you may stay in a blind spot where the driver cannot see you. Instead, pass promptly and safely, and avoid lingering alongside large vehicles.

question: If you're about to be struck from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Bracing yourself by pressing against the seat back.,b:Releasing your seat belt.,c:Pressing your head against the head restraint.
note: In a rear-end collision, your seat belt and head restraint protect you from serious injury. Never release your seat belt. To reduce whiplash, press your back firmly against the seat and your head against the head restraint while keeping the belt fastened.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop.,b:Maintain your normal speed.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield and enter the intersection only when it is safe.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, you should:
options: a:Only slow down if you see ice.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Drive at the posted speed.,d:Speed up to avoid hydroplaning.
note: On wet, snowy, or icy roads, your tires have less traction and it is easier to lose control. Reduce your speed and increase your following distance so you have more time and space to stop or steer smoothly.

question: What is the term used for the amount of alcohol in a person's bloodstream?
options: a:Implied consent (IC).,b:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).,c:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is the standard measure of how much alcohol is in a person’s bloodstream. As BAC increases, judgment, reaction time, and coordination are increasingly impaired, raising the risk of a crash.

question: When driving at night you should:
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: At night your ability to see and judge distance is reduced, so you should increase your following distance to give yourself more time to react. Use high beams only when there is no oncoming traffic and no vehicle directly ahead of you, and switch to low beams when other vehicles are nearby to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: Why should you use headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?
options: a:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,b:So others can see your vehicle.,c:To keep your engine warm.,d:To improve fuel economy.
note: Headlights increase your vehicle's visibility to other drivers in low-visibility weather; if wipers are required, low beams must also be used.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, which actions are required?
options: a:Check your blind spots and mirrors, and signal your intention.,b:Only signal and then change lanes.,c:Check mirrors but don't signal if traffic is light.
note: Before changing lanes or passing, always signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Mirrors alone cannot show you everything around your vehicle, so a quick head check helps you see vehicles that may be hidden and prevents sideswipe collisions.

question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, you should use:
options: a:Fog lights only.,b:High beams.,c:Low beams.
note: In fog, rain, or snow, use low beam headlights. High beams can reflect off moisture in the air and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams provide better forward visibility and make your vehicle more visible to others without blinding them.

question: If your vehicle begins to lose traction on a wet road, you should:
options: a:Drive at a constant speed to regain traction.,b:Apply the brakes firmly to stop sliding.,c:Slow down gradually without applying the brakes.
note: If you begin to lose traction or hydroplane on a wet road, ease off the accelerator and slow down gradually without braking or making sudden steering movements. This allows your tires to regain contact with the road surface and helps you maintain control of the vehicle.

question: If you start feeling drowsy while driving, you should:
options: a:Try to fight it until you reach your destination.,b:Take a break to rest or change drivers.,c:Take caffeine pills to stay awake.
note: If you feel drowsy while driving, you are already impaired. The safest action is to get off the road at a safe place and rest, nap, or switch drivers. Trying to fight sleep with tricks like opening windows or using caffeine is not reliable and can lead to falling asleep at the wheel.

question: What can happen if you mix a prescription drug with alcohol?
options: a:There will likely be no effect.,b:It will make you more alert.,c:It can make you unfit to drive.
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines can cause drowsiness, slowed reaction time, or other side effects. When combined with alcohol, these effects are often stronger and less predictable, making you unsafe and legally unfit to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed in a no-passing zone, you should:
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Slow down and let the other driver safely return to the drive lane.
note: If another driver is passing you, especially in a risky place like a no‑passing zone, your job is to help avoid a collision. Stay in your lane and, if needed, gently slow down so the passing driver has more space and time to return to the lane safely. Do not speed up or make sudden moves.

question: To reduce the chance of skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:
options: a:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,b:Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.,c:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
note: On wet, icy, or otherwise slippery roads, sudden braking or turning can cause a skid. Slow down before you reach curves and intersections so you can steer and brake gently and smoothly through them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If no signs or markings control turns at an intersection, you should turn into which lane?
options: a:Into the last available lane.,b:Into any lane.,c:Into the first available lane.
note: When turning at an intersection without specific lane‑use signs or markings, you should turn into the first legal lane going your direction. This keeps traffic organized and reduces conflicts with vehicles turning from the opposite direction.

question: If you approach an intersection at the posted speed and the signal turns yellow, you should:
options: a:Speed up to cross before it turns red.,b:Slow down and proceed through the intersection without caution.,c:Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through with caution rather than braking hard in the intersection.

question: If you see pedestrians waiting to use a crosswalk ahead, what must you do?
options: a:Continue because you have the right-of-way.,b:Pull to the right and go around them.,c:Wait for the pedestrians to finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk and wait until they have cleared the road before proceeding.

question: If you want to pass a pedestrian and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, you should:
options: a:Honk to get the pedestrian to move over.,b:Keep driving at the same speed; the oncoming vehicle must stop.,c:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before passing the pedestrian.
note: When a pedestrian and an oncoming vehicle are both ahead, you should not try to squeeze between them. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first, then pass the pedestrian only when you have enough clear space and it is safe.

question: When following a motorcycle you should:
options: a:Allow a larger following distance than you would for a car.,b:Be ready to use your horn frequently.,c:Drive more slowly than usual.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and can stop or swerve more quickly than cars. Leave at least a three- to four-second following distance so you have enough time to see them and react safely.

question: At a school crossing sign you should:
options: a:Always stop no matter what.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: A school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing the road. Slow down, watch carefully on both sides, and be prepared to stop whenever children are in or near the crosswalk.

question: If you have a tire blowout while driving, you should:
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.,b:Tap or pump the brakes repeatedly.,c:Slow down gradually and use the brakes lightly when needed.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, do not slam on the brakes, and ease your foot off the accelerator so the vehicle slows gradually. Once you have the vehicle under control and your speed has dropped, brake gently as needed and steer to a safe place off the road.

question: What does a 'No passing zone' sign indicate?
options: a:It is not safe and not legal to pass in this area.,b:You should speed up slightly.,c:You should maintain a steady speed.
note: A 'No passing zone' sign means you must not pass other vehicles in that area. These zones are placed where visibility is limited or road conditions make passing especially dangerous, so you must stay in your lane until the restriction ends.

question: A double solid yellow centerline indicates what about passing?
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Not allowed from either direction.
note: A double solid yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross the lines only when making a left turn or when allowed by specific markings, but not to pass another moving vehicle.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, you should:
options: a:Switch to high beams to see better.,b:Glance toward the right edge of the road.,c:Flash your lights repeatedly.
note: When oncoming headlights are too bright, do not look directly at them. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the road edge or lane markings as a guide while using your peripheral vision to monitor the road ahead.

question: Which foot should you use for both braking and accelerating?
options: a:Use your left foot to brake.,b:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating your vehicle.,c:You should always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.
note: In normal passenger vehicles with automatic or manual transmissions, you should use your right foot for both the accelerator and the brake. This helps prevent accidentally pressing both pedals at once and allows smoother, more controlled starts and stops.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of drug?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:An antihistamine.,c:A depressant.
note: Alcohol is classified as a depressant because it slows down activity in the central nervous system. This reduces judgment, coordination, and reaction time, making driving unsafe even at relatively low blood alcohol levels.

question: Driving more slowly than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:Appropriate in bad weather, but often a hazard when done unnecessarily.,b:Appropriate if you don't know the speed limit.,c:Always a safe defensive technique.
note: Driving much slower than surrounding traffic on a clear road can be dangerous because it disrupts traffic flow and may cause other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly. It is appropriate to slow down in bad weather or hazardous conditions, but driving significantly under the speed of traffic for no good reason can increase the risk of a crash.

question: Which of the following is a recommended safe driving technique?
options: a:Using your high beam lights in fog.,b:Staring at the road directly ahead for long periods.,c:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan their surroundings. Checking your mirrors every few seconds helps you stay aware of vehicles behind and beside you so you can react early to hazards. Staring straight ahead or using high beams in fog both reduce safety and visibility.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right, you should:
options: a:Squeeze between the truck and curb to make your turn.,b:Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.,c:Quickly turn inside the truck to beat it to the corner.
note: Large trucks and buses need extra room to turn and may swing wide before turning right. Never try to squeeze between a large vehicle and the curb or race it to the corner. Stay behind and wait until the truck or bus has completed its turn before you make yours.

question: If another vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, what is the first response you should take?
options: a:Honk and step on the brake firmly.,b:Swerve into the lane next to you.,c:Take your foot off the gas pedal.
note: If a vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, the safest first step is to ease off the accelerator. This gently increases your following distance without sudden braking or swerving, which could cause a rear-end collision or loss of control. Brake more firmly only if needed to avoid a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about driving too slowly is true?
options: a:The speed you choose does not affect safety.,b:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,c:Driving too slowly is never unsafe.
note: Driving much slower than surrounding traffic can be dangerous because it forces other drivers to brake or make sudden lane changes and risky passing maneuvers. You should generally travel at the speed of traffic, as long as it is within the posted speed limit and safe for conditions.

question: Drivers must obey instructions from which persons in construction areas?
options: a:Drivers who are broken down on the roadway.,b:Security guards in parking lots.,c:Flaggers (signal persons).
note: In construction and work zones, you must obey the instructions of flaggers (also called signal persons). They are authorized to direct traffic and their directions must be followed, even if they differ from traffic signals or signs, to protect workers and drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being tailgated on a two-lane road, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.,b:Apply your brakes to slow down, then resume your original speed.,c:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the other car.
note: If you are being tailgated and cannot safely change lanes, gradually slowing down can increase your following distance ahead and encourage the tailgater to pass when it is safe. Avoid sudden braking or speeding up, as both can increase the risk of a collision.

question: When merging onto a freeway, you should be driving:
options: a:At or near the speed of freeway traffic.,b:More slowly than the freeway traffic.,c:At the posted legal speed even if traffic is slower.
note: When merging onto a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of freeway traffic, as long as it is within the legal limit and safe. Matching speed allows you to merge smoothly and reduces the need for other drivers to brake or swerve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: May drivers pass another vehicle using the shoulder of the road?
options: a:When the shoulder is paved.,b:When the other vehicle is waiting to turn left.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You must not use the shoulder to pass another vehicle. The shoulder is not a travel lane and is reserved for emergencies, breakdowns, and sometimes for authorized vehicles. Passing on the shoulder is unsafe and illegal in most situations because other drivers do not expect moving traffic there.

question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol from the body?
options: a:Drink strong coffee.,b:Wait.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Only time allows the body to remove alcohol; coffee, food, or showers do not speed the elimination of alcohol.

question: Alcohol, in any concentration, is:
options: a:A stimulant.,b:A depressant.,c:Neither.
note: Alcohol is classified as a central nervous system depressant. It slows brain activity, reaction time, and coordination, which makes driving more dangerous even at relatively low blood alcohol levels.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From where should you begin a left turn when turning from a two-way street?
options: a:On the left of the centerline.,b:Near the centerline.,c:Near the right-hand side of the road.
note: When turning left from a two‑way street, you should start from the lane closest to the centerline. This position shortens the turn, keeps you out of oncoming traffic, and lines you up to enter the proper lane on the new road.

question: Which commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Exceeding the posted speed limit or driving too fast for conditions.,b:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,c:Scanning the environment and staying focused on driving.
note: Driving faster than the posted speed limit or too fast for weather, traffic, or road conditions greatly increases your stopping distance and crash risk. Safe drivers adjust their speed to match current conditions, even if that means driving below the speed limit.

question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake.,c:Leave the front wheels straight.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will gently touch the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving ability?
options: a:Three,b:Two,c:One
note: Even a single alcoholic drink can begin to affect coordination, judgment, and reaction time. Because you cannot know exactly how your body will respond, the safest rule is to assume that any amount of alcohol can impair your driving ability.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,b:They are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side.,c:Blind spots can be checked by using only your rearview mirrors.
note: All vehicles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show, but large trucks have much bigger blind areas on all sides. Drivers should avoid lingering alongside or close behind trucks where the truck driver may not see them, and should never rely on mirrors alone to check blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a red light with a green arrow displayed for your lane, when may you proceed?
options: a:Only after coming to a complete stop first.,b:Only after the arrow changes to green with no other signal.,c:When you are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.
note: A green arrow is a protected turn signal that allows you to proceed only in the direction of the arrow when you are in the proper lane and the intersection and crosswalk are clear. You do not need to stop first unless required by a sign or other condition, but you must always yield to any traffic or pedestrians still in the intersection.

question: Why is driving at night more hazardous than daytime driving?
options: a:Your reaction time is slower at night.,b:The road surface is always more slippery at night.,c:You cannot see as far ahead at night.
note: At night, your headlights limit how far ahead you can see, and glare from other vehicles can further reduce visibility. Because you cannot see as far ahead as in daylight, you have less time to react, so you should slow down and use extra caution.

question: Which substances can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, sedatives, and some cough/cold medications.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only prescription medications.
note: Many substances can impair driving, including tranquilizers, sedatives, marijuana, some prescription drugs, and over‑the‑counter cough or cold medicines that cause drowsiness. Both legal and illegal drugs can affect alertness, coordination, and judgment, so always read labels and follow medical advice before driving.

question: Which action can help reduce incidents of road rage?
options: a:Talk on your cell phone while driving.,b:Use your horn frequently to express frustration.,c:Always signal your intention when changing lanes.
note: Using your turn signals and driving courteously helps other drivers understand your intentions and reduces misunderstandings. Clear communication and calm, predictable driving are key ways to prevent road rage incidents.

question: Why is it dangerous to make sudden stops in front of large trucks or buses?
options: a:Small vehicle drivers cannot see large vehicles in their mirrors.,b:Large trucks and buses require longer stopping distances than passenger cars.,c:Large trucks and buses travel at higher speeds than cars.
note: Large trucks and buses are much heavier than passenger cars and need a longer distance to stop. If you suddenly stop in front of them, they may not be able to brake in time, greatly increasing the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: On gravel or dirt roads, your tires:
options: a:Have less traction than on pavement, so slow down.,b:Grip the road better than on pavement.,c:Provide better visibility than on pavement.
note: On gravel or dirt, the surface is loose and your tires cannot grip as well as on pavement. This reduced traction makes it easier to skid and harder to stop, so you should slow down and drive smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are facing a green light but the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,b:Turn left and find another route.,c:Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless there is enough space for your vehicle to completely clear it, even if the light is green. Entering and then blocking the intersection is unsafe and can be illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers making left turns must yield to:
options: a:Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.,b:Passing cars only.,c:No specific vehicles.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, including motorcycles and bicycles. Only turn when it is safe and there is a sufficient gap in oncoming traffic.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights approaches, you should:
options: a:Pull to the right side of the road and stop.,b:Continue driving but stay out of its way.,c:Try to reach your destination before it catches up to you.
note: When an emergency vehicle using lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping. This creates a clear path so the emergency vehicle can pass quickly and safely. Stay stopped until it has passed, unless a police officer directs otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk, what should you do?
options: a:Change lanes and pass the stopped vehicle.,b:Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have crossed.,c:Cautiously pass at 10 mph or slower.
note: If the driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk, you must not pass that vehicle because pedestrians may be crossing where you cannot see them. You should also stop, then proceed only after you are sure all pedestrians have completely cleared the crosswalk and it is safe to go.

question: A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02 percent typically does what to crash risk?
options: a:Has no effect on driving.,b:Won't put other drivers at risk.,c:Increases your risk of being in a crash, even though it is still below the usual legal limit for adults.
note: Any amount of alcohol in your system can impair driving, and crash risk begins to rise even at low BAC levels like 0.02%. However, the risk does not "nearly double" at 0.02%. Research shows a clear increase in crash risk as BAC rises, with much larger increases as BAC approaches and exceeds 0.08%. The safest and legal choice for drivers under 21, and the safest choice for all drivers, is to not drive after drinking any alcohol.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is an important step to perform before making a turn?
options: a:Check traffic in all directions and adjust your speed as needed.,b:Always move to the left lane before turning.,c:Increase your speed right before the turn.
note: Before making a turn, you should check traffic in all directions, use your mirrors and, when needed, check blind spots. Signal your turn well in advance and adjust your speed by slowing to a safe turning speed before you reach the intersection or driveway. This gives other road users time to react and helps you keep control through the turn.

question: If you are already in an intersection when a green light turns to yellow, you should:
options: a:Stop.,b:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,c:Increase your speed to avoid an accident.
note: A yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should continue through and clear the intersection safely rather than stopping suddenly. Stopping in the intersection can confuse other drivers and increase the risk of a collision.

question: Slowing down just to look at a crash or other unusual event typically:
options: a:Causes traffic congestion.,b:Prevents rear-end collisions.,c:Improves traffic flow.
note: Slowing down just to look at a crash, known as rubbernecking, disrupts normal traffic flow and often causes sudden braking. This creates congestion and increases the chance of rear-end and secondary collisions. Stay focused on the road ahead and maintain a safe, steady speed unless you must slow for safety or directions from officials.

question: What is the only thing that will reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Eating foods high in fat.,b:Drinking caffeine.,c:Time.,d:Taking a cold shower.
note: Only time allows your body to metabolize and eliminate alcohol; nothing speeds up the process.

question: Before driving, remove snow, frost, and ice from:
options: a:Just the windshield.,b:All windows.,c:Just the windshield and passenger window.
note: You must be able to see clearly in all directions before driving. Snow, frost, or ice on any window or mirror can create blind spots and make it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, or hazards. Always clear all windows and mirrors completely, not just a small area on the windshield.

question: Why should you leave extra space in front of a large truck?
options: a:To allow other drivers to merge onto the freeway.,b:To give the truck driver enough space to stop safely.,c:To allow other drivers more room when they want to slow down.
note: Large trucks are much heavier than passenger cars and need a longer distance to stop. Leaving extra space in front of a truck gives the truck driver enough room to slow or stop safely if traffic changes. Never cut closely in front of a truck and then brake; always allow a generous following and stopping distance around large vehicles.

question: A broken yellow centerline on the roadway means what regarding passing?
options: a:Passing on the left is allowed when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is never permitted.,c:Passing on the right is permitted at any time.
note: A broken yellow centerline means traffic on either side may pass on the left when it is safe and the way ahead is clear. You must still check for oncoming traffic, ensure you have enough distance to complete the pass, and obey any additional signs or markings that restrict passing in certain areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate highway, what is the proper procedure?
options: a:Select a safe gap in traffic and merge smoothly into the lane.,b:Always stop on the ramp before entering the highway.,c:Merge across two lanes at once to speed up.
note: On an interstate entrance ramp, use the acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge into a safe gap without stopping. Only stop if traffic or conditions make it absolutely necessary.

question: When you approach an octagonal sign, you must:
options: a:Stop.,b:Slow.,c:Turn.
note: An octagonal sign is always a STOP sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, yield to any pedestrians and vehicles with the right-of-way, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: On a freeway, why should you look farther ahead than on a city street?
options: a:To see potential hazards earlier and anticipate changes in traffic.,b:Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your vehicle completely.,c:Because it helps you keep up with traffic speed.
note: On freeways, speeds are higher, so situations develop more quickly. Looking farther ahead lets you spot slow traffic, lane closures, or hazards early so you can adjust speed or change lanes smoothly instead of making sudden maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, you must do what?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is near enough to cause conflict.,b:Always slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Yield only to vehicles approaching from your right.
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. Yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection or roadway. Proceed only when you can enter without forcing others to slow or stop suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road, you should:
options: a:Flash headlights to signal your pass.,b:Sound your horn while passing.,c:Judge distance and speed of oncoming vehicles before passing.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, check that the passing zone is legal and clear, and carefully judge the speed and distance of oncoming traffic and the vehicle you are passing. Only move into the opposing lane if you have enough time and space to pass safely and return to your lane.

question: As your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) rises, you become:
options: a:More coordinated.,b:More sober.,c:More intoxicated.
note: As blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, your judgment, coordination, and reaction time get worse. This means you become more impaired and more intoxicated, even if you feel “okay.”

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: After passing, stay in the left lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your inside rearview mirror. That distance helps ensure you have enough space before moving back into the right lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to enter a freeway, how should you check for traffic?
options: a:Use your rearview and side mirrors only.,b:Use only your rearview mirror.,c:Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to check blind spots.
note: When entering a freeway, use your mirrors and also turn your head to look over your shoulder. This shoulder check lets you see vehicles in your blind spots that mirrors alone cannot show.

question: What can continuous hard braking on snow and ice cause?
options: a:Locking of the front wheels and loss of steering control.,b:Faster stopping, reducing crash risk.,c:Prevention of brakes from freezing.
note: On snow and ice, hard continuous braking can cause your wheels to lock, which makes you lose steering control and can lead to a skid. Slow down early and brake gently so the tires keep rolling and you can still steer.

question: When backing up, you should:
options: a:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,b:Look through the rear window while reversing.,c:Press the gas gently to control movement.
note: When backing up, turn your body and look directly through the rear window so you have the clearest view of what is behind you. Move slowly and do not rely only on mirrors or cameras, which can miss hazards.

question: Under low-visibility conditions due to fog, you should:
options: a:Turn on your high beam headlights.,b:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,c:Increase your speed so you clear the area quickly.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights because high beams reflect off the moisture droplets and create glare, making it even harder to see. You should slow down so you have more time to react to hazards, and if visibility becomes extremely poor, pull off the road to a safe location and wait until conditions improve.

question: You should always travel at:
options: a:The speed of vehicles surrounding you.,b:The posted speed limit regardless of conditions.,c:A speed appropriate for the road and weather conditions.
note: You must adjust your speed to match road, traffic, and weather conditions while staying at or below the posted speed limit. If conditions are poor, it is often safer and legally required to drive below the posted limit so you can stop and maneuver safely.

question: To avoid losing traction on wet roads you should:
options: a:Make abrupt turns.,b:Apply the brakes firmly.,c:Slow down.
note: On wet roads, slowing down helps your tires maintain better contact with the road and reduces the risk of hydroplaning. Avoid sudden steering, braking, or acceleration, because abrupt actions can cause you to lose traction when the road is slick.

question: If your vehicle's suspension is worn, it can cause:
options: a:Vehicle control problems.,b:Squealing brakes only.,c:Steering slack only.
note: A worn suspension system can reduce your ability to control the vehicle, especially when turning, braking, or driving over bumps. It affects stability, steering response, and tire contact with the road, increasing the risk of losing control and should be repaired promptly.

question: Which of the following is a dangerous driving habit in work zones?
options: a:Tailgating another vehicle only.,b:Failing to carefully watch for workers and equipment only.,c:Both tailgating and failing to watch for workers/machines.
note: In work zones, both tailgating and failing to watch carefully for workers and equipment are dangerous. Traffic may stop or slow suddenly, and workers or machinery can move into your path unexpectedly, so you must leave extra following distance, reduce speed, and stay highly alert.

question: Double solid yellow centerlines indicate that passing is:
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Allowed only from your direction.,c:Not allowed from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines mean vehicles in both directions are prohibited from crossing the lines to pass. You must stay in your lane and may only cross these lines when making a permitted left turn or U-turn where it is otherwise legal, not for passing.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?
options: a:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,b:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.,c:Any prescription drug is safe if you don't feel drowsy.
note: Many medicines, including some over-the-counter cold, allergy, and pain medicines, can make you drowsy, dizzy, or less alert and can impair driving. It is illegal to drive under the influence of any drug—legal or illegal—that affects your ability to drive safely. Always read labels and talk to your doctor or pharmacist before driving.

question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:At all times; do everything possible to avoid striking a pedestrian.,b:Only if they are in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only if traffic signals favor the pedestrian.
note: Drivers must always use extreme care around pedestrians and do everything reasonably possible to avoid hitting them, even if the pedestrian is crossing illegally. You must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks (marked or unmarked) and be prepared to stop whenever you see a pedestrian who may enter your path.

question: Which statement best describes a driver license?
options: a:Requirement.,b:Privilege, not a right.,c:Right, not a privilege.
note: A driver license is a legal privilege granted by the state, not an automatic right. You must meet requirements such as passing tests, obeying traffic laws, and maintaining safe driving behavior to keep this privilege. The state can suspend or revoke your license if you violate the rules.

question: Upon seeing orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you should:
options: a:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.,b:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.,c:Slow down because the lane ends ahead.,d:Ignore the signs and cones.
note: Orange signs and cones indicate a work zone. You should slow down, be alert for workers, equipment, lane shifts, and sudden stops, and follow posted work-zone speed limits. Be prepared to change lanes or stop if necessary, and drive with extra caution through the area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to make a left turn on red after stopping?
options: a:Only when you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.,b:When you are on a two-way street turning onto a two-way street.,c:Whenever you yield to traffic.
note: In most U.S. states, you may turn left on red only when turning from a one‑way street onto another one‑way street, after coming to a complete stop and yielding to traffic and pedestrians, and only if there is no sign prohibiting the turn.

question: How do sudden wind gusts on highways affect vehicles?
options: a:They can cause problems for all vehicles.,b:They only affect large vehicles.,c:They only cause visibility problems.
note: Sudden wind gusts can push any vehicle sideways, especially at highway speeds, and can also blow dust, snow, or debris that reduces visibility. Drivers of all vehicles must be prepared to steer and adjust speed when winds are strong.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.,b:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:After about three seconds.
note: After passing, you should not move back into the right lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your inside rearview mirror. This shows you have enough space to return without cutting the other driver off.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.,b:Yield only to vehicles on your right.,c:Never stop when approaching a yield sign.
note: At a yield sign, slow down and be ready to stop. You must let traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the lane you want to enter go first if they are close enough to be a hazard, proceeding only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, you should:
options: a:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.,b:Slow down.,c:Check the inside rearview mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. This head check lets you see into your blind spot to be sure no vehicle is hidden there.

question: If you encounter a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, you should:
options: a:Expect them to yield to you.,b:Yield the right-of-way to them.,c:Honk to warn them of your presence.
note: Blind or visually impaired pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog always have the right-of-way. You must stop or yield as needed, never honk at them unnecessarily, and give them extra time and space to cross safely.

question: Why is night driving more challenging?
options: a:There are fewer cars on the road at night.,b:The speed limit is increased at night.,c:Because it is harder to judge distance and the speed of other vehicles in the dark.
note: At night, your visibility is limited mostly to the area lit by your headlights. This reduced visibility makes it harder to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are moving, so you must drive more cautiously.

question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, what is required of drivers?
options: a:Stop when the bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, unless you are on the opposite side of a divided highway with a physical median.,b:Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction as the bus, even on undivided roads.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, drivers in both directions must stop on undivided roads until the lights stop and the arm is withdrawn. On a divided highway with a physical median, only traffic traveling in the same direction as the bus must stop; oncoming traffic on the other side of the median may proceed with caution.

question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:To better see around the sides of the vehicle.,b:Because drivers often pull behind large vehicles before passing.,c:To avoid being caught in the vehicle's slipstream.
note: Large trucks and buses block your view of the road ahead and have large blind spots. By increasing your following distance, you can see more of the road around them, have more time to react, and stay out of their blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Changing lanes from one lane to another should be done:
options: a:Quickly and often.,b:When a car is in your blind spot.,c:Gradually and carefully.
note: Lane changes should be made only when necessary and done smoothly. Always signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check blind spots, then move gradually and carefully into the new lane.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with no safety barrier, you should:
options: a:Quickly cross if it looks like you can beat the train.,b:Assume no trains cross there.,c:Cross only after looking both directions for an oncoming train.
note: At an unprotected railroad crossing, you must slow down, look and listen in both directions, and be prepared to stop. Never try to beat a train; trains are much faster and need a long distance to stop. Only cross when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Call your insurance company when you get home.,b:Wait for the owner to return.,c:Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner, you are legally required to leave a clearly written note with your name, address, and contact information securely on the vehicle, and report the collision as required by local law. This allows the owner and insurance companies to handle the damages properly.

question: When is highway pavement most slippery during rainfall?
options: a:Just after the rain begins.,b:After it has been raining several hours.,c:After one to two hours of rain.
note: Pavement is usually most slippery at the beginning of a rainstorm. Oil, grease, and dust that have built up on the road mix with the first water and create a slick film. After it has rained for a while, much of this residue is washed away and traction generally improves, though you should still drive carefully.

question: Why are roads often more hazardous right after it begins to rain?
options: a:Because the mix of oil and water on the road reduces traction.,b:Because heavy rain always makes roads less slippery than light rain.,c:Because you should avoid making fast turns or stops until road traction improves.
note: Right after rain begins, oil and other residues on the road surface mix with the water and make the pavement very slick. Because traction is reduced, you should slow down and avoid quick turns, hard braking, or sudden lane changes until the road surface has been washed clean and traction improves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic while your light is green, what is the best action?
options: a:Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.,b:Do not enter the intersection until you can get completely across.,c:Partially enter the intersection to establish right-of-way.
note: A green light does not give you the right to block an intersection. You must wait behind the crosswalk or stop line until there is enough space on the far side for your vehicle to clear the intersection completely. Entering and stopping in the intersection can block cross traffic and is illegal in many areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what should you do to check for traffic?
options: a:Rely only on the side mirror.,b:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot.,c:Rely solely on the rearview mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. This head check lets you see into your blind spot, where vehicles may not appear in your mirrors.

question: On a slippery road, how should your following distance compare to normal?
options: a:Maintain a greater distance from the vehicle ahead than normal.,b:Keep the same following distance as normal.,c:Follow closer to the car ahead than normal.
note: On wet, icy, or otherwise slippery roads, your stopping distance increases. Leave more space than usual between your vehicle and the one ahead so you have extra time and distance to brake smoothly and avoid skids.

question: Orange-colored traffic signs typically indicate:
options: a:School zone signs.,b:Work zone signs.,c:Regulatory signs.,d:Guide signs.
note: Orange traffic signs are used for temporary traffic control in work zones. They warn of construction, maintenance, or utility work and alert you to slow down, be prepared for lane shifts, and watch for workers and equipment.

question: When driving in heavy fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights so the light aims down at the road instead of reflecting back at you. High beams create glare in fog and make it harder to see. If visibility is extremely poor, pull off the road to a safe place and wait until conditions improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which sign indicates when it is safe to return to your lane after passing?
options: a:You have passed the other vehicle’s front bumper.,b:You cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.,c:You see the vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can clearly see the headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead of that vehicle and reduces the risk of cutting it off.

question: A flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection means you should do what?
options: a:Stop, then enter when safe.,b:Yield to all traffic before crossing the intersection.,c:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down, look carefully for other vehicles and pedestrians, and proceed through the intersection only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:The same as a yield sign.,b:The same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.,c:The light is about to turn green.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, proceed only when traffic and pedestrians are clear and it is safe to go.

question: If confronted by an aggressive driver, what is the safest action?
options: a:Challenge them.,b:Get out of their way.,c:Speed up.
note: When another driver is aggressive, the safest response is to avoid any confrontation. Slow down if needed, let them pass, and create space so you are not near their vehicle.

question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Drive on the interstate to let off steam.,b:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.,c:Play loud music so you won’t think about your argument.,d:Call someone while driving to calm down.
note: Strong emotions like anger reduce your concentration and judgment. Before driving, take time to calm down so you can focus fully on the road and make safe decisions.

question: Which color is most commonly used for regulatory signs?
options: a:White.,b:Yellow.,c:Green.
note: Regulatory signs, such as speed limit, no parking, and lane use signs, are most often white rectangles with black, red, or green symbols or lettering that tell you what you must or must not do.

question: How should you reduce the risk of hydroplaning in rainy weather?
options: a:Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,b:Decrease your speed.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. The most effective way to reduce this risk is to slow down in wet conditions and drive smoothly so your tires can maintain traction.

question: Which of the following describes how alcohol and drugs affect driving skills?
options: a:Reaction time and coordination.,b:Driving ability is unaffected.,c:All of the above.,d:Alertness and concentration.
note: Alcohol and many drugs depress the central nervous system. They reduce alertness and concentration and also slow reaction time and harm coordination. Because alcohol and drugs affect all of these skills, any amount can make driving unsafe.

question: What is the best practice to avoid dangerous situations while driving?
options: a:Turn off the radio.,b:Always keep your eyes focused only ahead of your car.,c:Be aware of what is happening around your vehicle.
note: To avoid dangerous situations, you must constantly be aware of your surroundings. Scan ahead, to the sides, and behind you so you can spot hazards early and adjust your speed or lane position before they become emergencies.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Arkansas, what are shared center lanes used for?
options: a:To accelerate after turning left only.,b:To make left turns from either direction.,c:To pass slower traffic.
note: A shared center turn lane is reserved only for vehicles making left turns from either direction or for vehicles entering the roadway to merge into traffic after a left turn. It is not for passing or for driving long distances.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way road that has no curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead,b:Right, toward the side of the road.,c:Left, toward the center of the road.
note: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the right, toward the edge of the road. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from traffic instead of into the lane.

question: You should allow an extra cushion of space when following which driver?
options: a:A driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle (such as truck/bus pulling trailer).,b:A station wagon.,c:A small passenger car.
note: You should leave extra following distance behind large vehicles or those towing trailers because they often have large blind spots and limited rear visibility. The extra space gives you more time to react and makes it easier to see around them and stop safely if they brake suddenly.

question: Tailgating, or following another vehicle too closely, can:
options: a:Cannot result in a traffic citation.,b:Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.,c:Is required when traffic is heavy.,d:Reduce collisions by preventing being cut off.
note: Tailgating is following another vehicle too closely. It increases the risk of rear‑end collisions and often angers or frustrates other drivers, which can lead to aggressive driving. It is unsafe and can also result in a traffic citation, so you should always maintain a safe following distance.

question: When driving at night, what should you do to increase safety?
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at oncoming headlights.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: At night your visibility is reduced, so you need more time and space to react. Increasing your following distance gives you a larger safety cushion if the vehicle ahead stops or swerves suddenly. Avoid staring at oncoming headlights and use high beams only when appropriate and when they will not blind other drivers.

question: Which part of the roadway is most likely to become icy in cold weather after snow or rain?
options: a:A hilly, open road,b:A residential road,c:A road in a shaded area
note: Roads in shaded areas freeze sooner and stay icy longer because they receive less sunlight. Even when the rest of the road looks clear, shaded spots can still be slick, so slow down and be prepared for reduced traction in these areas.

question: What does a steady red arrow displayed on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Drivers may not proceed in the indicated direction until the arrow changes.,b:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after coming to a complete stop.,c:Drivers may proceed in the indicated direction with caution.
note: A steady red arrow means you must stop and may not go in the direction the arrow points until the signal changes to green (or a green arrow). It specifically prohibits movement in that direction, even if other movements at the intersection are allowed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, you should never:
options: a:Change lanes abruptly or without signaling.,b:Check for other vehicles moving into the same space.,c:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
note: When changing lanes, you must always signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check blind spots. The one thing you must never do is change lanes suddenly or without signaling, because this gives other drivers no time to react and greatly increases the risk of a collision.

question: If your vehicle becomes disabled on the highway, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Stop in the right lane.,b:Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway.,c:Stop where you are.
note: If your vehicle becomes disabled on a highway, you should, if possible, pull completely off the traveled portion of the road so all four wheels are off the pavement. This reduces the chance of being struck by passing traffic and gives you space to safely deal with the breakdown.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what is the correct action?
options: a:Stop immediately.,b:When safe, gradually steer back onto the roadway.,c:Turn immediately back onto the roadway.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and keep a firm grip on the wheel. When traffic is clear and your speed is under control, gradually steer back onto the roadway. Jerking the wheel or turning sharply can cause you to lose control or skid into other lanes.

question: Prior to entering a curve, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Activate your turn signal.,c:Brake hard into the curve.
note: Before entering a curve, slow down to a safe speed while your vehicle is still traveling straight. Braking hard in the curve can cause skidding or loss of control, especially on wet or slippery roads. Enter the curve at a controlled speed and then gently accelerate as you exit if conditions allow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must drivers obey posted speed limits?
options: a:Only in heavy traffic.,b:Only when police officers are present.,c:At all times.
note: Posted speed limits are the maximum legal speeds under ideal conditions and must be obeyed at all times, not just when traffic is heavy or police are nearby. You must also slow down further when conditions such as rain, fog, or heavy traffic make the posted speed unsafe.

question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, you should:
options: a:Glance briefly toward the right side of the road.,b:Stare at the centerline.,c:Flash your high beams.
note: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, briefly look toward the right edge of your lane instead of directly at the lights. Use the right side of the road and your peripheral vision to keep your lane position while avoiding being blinded by the glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When it comes to right-of-way, a driver should:
options: a:Assume all drivers will obey right-of-way rules automatically.,b:Assume most drivers obey the rules.,c:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way to avoid a collision.
note: Right-of-way rules help decide who goes first, but they do not guarantee that others will yield. Even when you legally have the right-of-way, you must be ready to slow, stop, or yield to avoid a collision. Safety always comes before insisting on your right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signal?
