options: a:Only when pulling away from the curb.,b:Only when pulling next to the curb.,c:When pulling next to or away from the curb.
note: Use your turn signal any time you change your position relative to traffic, including when pulling toward the curb to park and when leaving the curb to re-enter traffic. Signaling lets other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians anticipate your movement and adjust safely.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:Only if you are involved in a collision.,b:If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.,c:Only if you are stopped and cited.
note: You must carry proof of financial responsibility (usually an insurance card) and show it to law enforcement when requested, such as if you are involved in a collision or stopped for a traffic violation. Having it readily available helps verify that you are legally insured to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is merging into your freeway lane, you should:
options: a:Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.,b:Always maintain your position.,c:Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.
note: When vehicles are merging onto a freeway, you should help maintain a smooth, safe flow of traffic. If you can do so safely, adjust your speed or change lanes to create space so merging drivers can enter without sudden braking or dangerous lane changes.

question: When leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot across a sidewalk, what must drivers do?
options: a:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk area and yield to pedestrians.,b:Expect pedestrians to yield and only stop if they are blocking your path.,c:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
note: When exiting an alley, driveway, or parking lot across a sidewalk, you must stop before crossing the sidewalk area and look carefully for pedestrians. Pedestrians on the sidewalk have the right-of-way, and you must yield to them before you move forward.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, to whom should you yield?
options: a:Yield to any driver who arrived before you.,b:Yield to the driver on your left.,c:Yield to the vehicle across from you.
note: At a four-way stop, vehicles proceed in the order in which they arrive. If another driver reaches the intersection before you, you must yield to that driver. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights, where should you look?
options: a:Look toward the center of the roadway.,b:Look toward the right side of the road.,c:Look straight ahead.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly into the bright lights. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the right side of the road as a guide so you are not blinded and can keep your vehicle in your lane.

question: What does double solid yellow centerline signaling mean?
options: a:Neither direction may pass.,b:Both directions may pass.,c:The lane to the right may pass only.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means passing is not allowed for traffic in either direction. You may cross these lines only when making a permitted left turn or when instructed by traffic control, but you may not use the opposing lane to pass another vehicle.

question: Is it lawful to drive while impaired by medication that affects your ability to drive?
options: a:No — driving while impaired by medication is not permitted under any circumstances.,b:Yes if the medication was prescribed by a physician.,c:Yes if you do not feel drowsy.
note: Driving is illegal if you are impaired by any substance that affects your ability to drive safely, including prescription or over‑the‑counter medications. Even if a doctor prescribed it, you must not drive if the medication makes you drowsy, slows your reactions, or otherwise impairs your driving.

question: When stopped at a red light that shows a green arrow in your direction, you may proceed if:
options: a:You first come to a complete stop.,b:You wait until the other lights change.,c:You are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.
note: A green arrow is a protected turn signal. You may proceed in the direction of the arrow if you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear, while yielding to pedestrians and any vehicles already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive much slower than surrounding traffic, what is likely to happen?
options: a:You will most likely interfere with traffic and could be cited.,b:You will improve traffic flow.,c:You will demonstrate defensive driving techniques.
note: Driving significantly below the flow of traffic may block the normal and reasonable movement of traffic and can result in a citation. Try to match the speed of traffic within the legal limit.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. Vehicles on the side with the broken line may cross it to pass when it is safe. Vehicles on the side with the solid line must not cross it to pass.

question: A stopped school bus with red flashing lights means you must:
options: a:Stop and proceed when you think children are clear.,b:Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.,c:Remain stopped while the red lights flash.
note: When a school bus has red lights flashing, you must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and it is safe to proceed. This rule protects children who may be crossing the road. Some states allow an exception for oncoming traffic on a divided highway with a physical barrier between directions.

question: Which action helps prevent hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Put on cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,b:Slow down.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water instead of the road, usually at higher speeds on wet pavement. The best way to prevent hydroplaning is to slow down, especially when it first starts to rain or when water is pooling on the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: There are two lanes moving in your direction and you are in the left lane while vehicles are passing you on the right. If a driver behind wants to go faster, what should you do?
options: a:Move into the right lane when it is safe to do so.,b:Drive onto the left shoulder to let other vehicles pass.,c:Stay in your lane and not impede traffic.
note: On multi-lane roads, the left lane is generally for passing or faster traffic. If vehicles are passing you on the right and a driver behind you wants to go faster, you should safely move into the right lane when there is a clear gap. This keeps traffic flowing smoothly and reduces the risk of tailgating or aggressive driving.

question: When you see a pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog, what should you do?
options: a:Honk to alert them to your presence.,b:Allow them the right-of-way.,c:Quickly swerve around them.
note: A pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog is visually impaired and must be given the right-of-way at all times. Slow down or stop as needed and allow them to cross safely. Do not honk or try to drive around them, as this can startle or endanger them.

question: When following another vehicle at night, you should:
options: a:Use your high beam headlights.,b:Use your high beams until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.,c:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.
note: When driving at night and following another vehicle, use low beam headlights. High beams can reflect in the mirrors of the vehicle ahead and temporarily blind or distract that driver. Low beams provide enough light for you while keeping others safe and comfortable.

question: When adjusting your inside rearview mirror, you should position it so you can see:
options: a:The passengers in the backseat clearly.,b:The entire rear window.,c:Your own reflection for visibility.
note: Adjust the inside rearview mirror so you can see as much of the rear window as possible with only a slight movement of your eyes. This gives you the widest view of traffic behind you and helps you monitor vehicles approaching from the rear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when another vehicle is passing you?
options: a:Brake hard.,b:Speed up.,c:Maintain a constant speed.
note: When another vehicle is passing you, maintain a steady speed and stay in your lane. Do not speed up or brake suddenly, as this can make the pass unsafe. A constant speed helps the other driver judge distance and complete the pass safely.

question: Like alcohol or drugs, drowsiness can do what to your driving?
options: a:Make you feel better.,b:Help you be a better driver.,c:Impair your judgment.
note: Drowsy driving is dangerous because being very tired affects you much like alcohol or drugs. It reduces alertness, slows your reaction time, and impairs your judgment, making it harder to notice hazards and respond safely.

question: After a minor intersection collision with no injuries, you should:
options: a:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until law enforcement arrives.,b:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so.,c:Not move your vehicle for any reason.
note: After a minor crash with no injuries and drivable vehicles, you should move your car out of the traffic lane if it is safe. This helps prevent additional collisions and keeps traffic flowing while you exchange information and, if required, report the crash.

question: If pedestrians are crossing illegally in the middle of the street, what must you do?
options: a:Do not have to stop for them.,b:You must stop for them.,c:Proceed as usual.,d:Sound your horn to warn them.
note: Drivers must always do what is necessary to avoid hitting a pedestrian, even if the pedestrian is crossing illegally. If someone is in the roadway, you must slow or stop to avoid a collision and proceed only when it is safe.

question: What should you do when driving in fog?
options: a:Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.,b:Slow down and use your high beam headlights.,c:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
note: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. If visibility becomes extremely poor, pull off the road to a safe place and wait for conditions to improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view is blocked at an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain your speed and look both ways.,b:Slow down and look both ways.,c:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.
note: When your view is blocked at an intersection, stop first. Then slowly move forward until you can clearly see cross traffic in both directions. Only proceed when you are sure the way is clear and it is safe to enter.

question: If the centerline is a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line, passing is:
options: a:Permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.,b:Not permitted from either direction.,c:Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line. Drivers on the side with the solid line must not cross it to pass because it is considered unsafe from that direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you make room for vehicles entering a freeway?
options: a:Maintain your speed and position.,b:Merge into a different lane when possible and adjust your speed if you cannot change lanes.,c:Slow down only and stay in your lane.
note: When you see vehicles entering a freeway, you should help them merge safely. If it is safe, move over to another lane to give them space. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed—either slightly speed up or slow down—to create a safe gap for the entering vehicle.

question: What do yellow center lines separate?
options: a:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,b:Carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.,c:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
note: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads. They help you know where oncoming traffic will be and indicate whether passing is allowed based on whether the line is solid or broken.

question: If the road ahead is flooded, you should:
options: a:Drive only in the center of the roadway.,b:Not drive through it; turn around and find another route.,c:Slam on the brakes.
note: You should never drive through a flooded roadway. Water can be deeper or moving faster than it appears, can hide holes or debris, and can quickly sweep a vehicle away. Turn around and find another route.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When would it be illegal to start across an intersection?
options: a:You may enter only if there is room to clear the intersection on a green light.,b:You must not enter if you will block the intersection under any circumstances.,c:You may not enter even during heavy traffic if you cannot clear the intersection.,d:You may enter on a yellow light only if you can clear the intersection without blocking it.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless there is enough space to completely clear it, even if the light is green or yellow. Entering when you cannot get all the way through can block cross traffic and is illegal in many areas.

question: If an oncoming vehicle's high beams are blinding you at night, you should:
options: a:Look straight ahead in your lane.,b:Look toward the right edge of your lane and avoid staring.,c:Look toward the left edge of your lane.
note: When an oncoming driver fails to dim their high beams, do not stare into the bright lights. Instead, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the lane line or road edge as a guide. This reduces glare and helps you maintain your lane position while still using your peripheral vision to monitor the other vehicle.

question: When crossing a sidewalk entering or exiting a driveway, drivers should:
options: a:Claim the right-of-way.,b:Yield to pedestrians.,c:Sound the horn to get pedestrians to move.
note: When you cross a sidewalk to enter or exit a driveway, pedestrians have the right-of-way. You must slow or stop as needed and allow people walking, using wheelchairs, or with strollers to pass safely before you drive across the sidewalk.

question: When a large truck ahead is making a right turn on a multi-lane street, the truck may:
options: a:Always stay in the right lane during the turn.,b:Have to swing wide to complete the right turn.,c:Complete the turn in either lane with equal ease.
note: Large trucks often need to swing wide to the left before turning right because their rear wheels follow a tighter path than the front wheels. Give them extra space and never try to squeeze between the truck and the curb when you see a truck preparing for or making a right turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter the freeway but cannot see a gap in traffic, you should:
options: a:Maintain your speed and force other drivers to create a gap.,b:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.
note: On most freeways, you should adjust your speed on the ramp so you can merge smoothly into traffic without stopping. However, if you reach the end of the ramp and still cannot find a safe gap, you must stop and wait until traffic clears enough to merge safely. Never force other drivers to brake or swerve to let you in.

question: When must you obey a school crossing guard's directions?
options: a:At all times while they are directing traffic.,b:Only during school hours.,c:Only if children are present.
note: School crossing guards have legal authority to direct traffic. You must obey their signals and instructions any time they are on duty and directing traffic, regardless of the exact time of day or whether you see children in the crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should drive the posted maximum speed limit only:
options: a:During the night.,b:During the day.,c:Under ideal conditions.
note: The posted maximum speed is the fastest you may legally drive only when conditions are ideal—good visibility, dry pavement, light traffic, and safe vehicle control. If weather, traffic, or road conditions are poor, you must drive slower than the posted maximum to be safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you give up your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Often, even at controlled intersections.,b:Whenever it helps prevent collisions.,c:Never; it confuses other drivers.
note: Right-of-way is never something you should insist on if it risks a crash. Even if you are legally entitled to go first, you should yield whenever it helps prevent a collision, because safety is more important than being “right.” Do not assume other drivers will follow the rules correctly.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, you should:
options: a:Open a window and keep driving.,b:Stop and either get rest or change drivers.,c:Drink something with caffeine and continue driving.
note: To avoid fatigued driving, stop and rest or switch drivers rather than relying on caffeine or fresh air.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On an interstate, how can you avoid traffic merging from on-ramps to your right?
options: a:Change lanes to the left when traffic permits.,b:Slow down.,c:Maintain your speed and position.
note: On interstates, vehicles enter from on-ramps on the right. To reduce conflicts and allow them room to merge, you should move to the left lane when it is safe and legal to do so. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed as needed to create a safe gap, but never maintain your position if it would cause a dangerous situation.

question: A pentagon-shaped traffic sign is used to indicate what?
options: a:A regulatory sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A school zone or school crossing.
note: Pentagon-shaped (five-sided) signs are used for school zones and school crossings. They alert drivers to areas where children may be walking or crossing the road so that drivers can slow down, watch carefully, and be prepared to stop.

question: What are "no zones" around large trucks?
options: a:Zones where it is safe to travel behind the truck.,b:Areas with several car lengths between vehicles.,c:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or restrict the truck's ability to stop and maneuver.
note: No-zones are the large blind spots and close-in areas around trucks where the driver may not see you or may not be able to stop or maneuver safely. Avoid lingering in these areas, especially directly behind, alongside the cab, and close in front of the truck.

question: What should you do when approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light?
options: a:Stop before crossing the intersection.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, yielding as necessary. You do not have to stop unless needed for other traffic, pedestrians, or to avoid a hazard.

question: On a multilane road where a dashed yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, who may pass?
options: a:Both directions may pass.,b:Only traffic next to the dashed line may pass.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.
note: When a dashed yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, only vehicles on the side with the dashed line may cross it to pass if it is safe. Vehicles on the solid-line side must not cross the line to pass.

question: When you encounter a pedestrian carrying a white cane or using a guide dog, how must you respond?
options: a:Only if a crossing guard is present.,b:Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.,c:Give them the right-of-way at all times.
note: A pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog is visually impaired and must be given the right-of-way at all times. Stop well before the crosswalk, do not honk or rev your engine, and allow them to cross safely and completely.

question: What is the only medically proven way to reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Allow your body time to metabolize the alcohol.,b:Drink coffee to sober up.,c:Take a cold shower to reduce BAC.
note: No food, drink, or activity speeds elimination of alcohol—only the passage of time lowers BAC.

question: To avoid injury from an airbag, how many inches should a driver sit from the steering wheel?
options: a:Approximately 10 inches.,b:About 20 inches.,c:About 15 inches.
note: Drivers should sit with their chest at least about 10 inches from the center of the steering wheel. This distance helps the airbag deploy properly and reduces the risk of injury from the force of the airbag while still allowing you to reach the controls comfortably.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drug use?
options: a:Coordination.,b:Both alertness and coordination.,c:Alertness.,d:None of the above.
note: Alcohol and many drugs slow your brain and body, affecting several skills at once. Your alertness, judgment, reaction time, and coordination all get worse, which makes it harder to notice hazards, steer smoothly, brake in time, and stay in your lane.

question: When can you legally go around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:When you can clearly see both directions.,b:Never.,c:When the warning lights are not flashing.
note: You must never drive around, under, or through a lowered railroad crossing gate, even if you do not see a train. Wait until the gates are fully raised and the warning lights and bells have stopped before crossing; trains can approach faster and be closer than they appear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When completing a pass, you have enough room to return to the driving lane when:
options: a:The other driver signals for you to re-enter.,b:You look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.,c:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing another vehicle, do not move back into the lane until you can see both of the passed vehicle’s headlights in your inside rearview mirror. This tells you there is enough space between your vehicle and the one you passed to return safely without cutting them off.

question: How do stopping distances and collision severity change as vehicle speed increases?
options: a:Decrease as speed increases.,b:Remain unchanged.,c:Increase as speed increases.
note: As speed increases, your vehicle needs a much longer distance to stop, and crash forces grow rapidly. Higher speeds make collisions more severe, so you must leave more following distance and slow down when conditions are not ideal.

question: When may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:When you are on a hill or curve.,b:When there is a solid line next to your lane.,c:When the centerline next to your lane is broken (dashed) and the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken (dashed) centerline next to your lane means you may pass if the lane is clear and it is safe. A solid line next to your lane means you must not cross it to pass, and you must never pass on hills or curves where you cannot see far enough ahead.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.,b:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down and proceed through the intersection with extra caution. You do not have to stop unless needed for safety or to yield to other traffic or pedestrians.

question: As daylight begins to fade, to help others see you, you should use:
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Emergency flashers.
note: As it starts to get dark, you should turn on your low beam headlights so other drivers can see you clearly. Parking lights or emergency flashers are not a substitute for headlights while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn prohibited?
options: a:In a parking lot.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:On a straight road with 500 feet clear view in both directions.
note: U‑turns are generally prohibited on or near hills and curves where your view of oncoming traffic is limited. You should only make a U‑turn where you have a clear view and it is specifically allowed by signs and local law.

question: If you refuse to take a lawful alcohol test when requested by an officer, what may happen?
options: a:You are simply exercising your rights as a motorist.,b:You may lose your driver's license.,c:There will be no consequences.
note: Under implied consent laws, by driving you agree to take a lawful alcohol test when requested. Refusing the test can lead to an automatic license suspension and other penalties, even if you are not convicted of DUI.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle traveling the same direction, how should you complete the maneuver?
options: a:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.,b:Pass as slowly as possible to minimize speed difference.,c:Pass as safely and as quickly as possible, then return to your lane when safe.
note: When passing, move into the passing lane, accelerate to safely and promptly overtake the other vehicle without exceeding the speed limit, and return to your lane only when you can see enough clear space ahead. Lingering beside another vehicle increases collision risk.

question: When a pedestrian is using a guide dog or carrying a white cane and is crossing, what must drivers do?
options: a:Always yield the right-of-way to that pedestrian.,b:Tell the pedestrian where to cross the street.,c:Only yield if you are at a corner.
note: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to blind or visually impaired pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane. Stop or remain stopped until they have safely crossed, and never honk, rush them, or try to direct them verbally from your vehicle.

question: A pedestrian started after the 'Don't Walk' signal and is in the street when your light turns green. What should you do?
options: a:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,b:Wait until the pedestrian has finished crossing before you proceed.,c:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
note: Even on a green light, you must yield to pedestrians who are in the intersection. Wait until they have crossed before you proceed.

question: When an oncoming car's headlights are very bright at night, you should:
options: a:Stop until the other driver passes.,b:Look below their headlights.,c:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.
note: At night, avoid looking directly at bright oncoming headlights. Briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road to use it as a guide while keeping track of your lane position until the vehicle passes.

question: If a vehicle has a two-part seat belt system, how should you use it?
options: a:Wear both the lap and shoulder belt together.,b:Use only the lap belt.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.
note: In a two-part seat belt system, always wear both the lap and shoulder belt. The lap belt should be low over the hips, and the shoulder belt across the chest and away from the neck. Using only one part greatly reduces protection in a crash.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, which is an expected behavior?
options: a:They may wait on the side of the road.,b:They may use the left lane.,c:They may cut through all lanes.
note: A bicyclist making a left turn has two safe, legal options: they may merge into and use the left turn lane like a motor vehicle, or they may stay to the right, cross the intersection, wait on the far side, and then cross again when safe. This second method is common for less-experienced riders, so you should expect that a bicyclist may wait on the side of the road to complete a left turn in two stages. Cutting straight across multiple lanes of moving traffic is unsafe and not an expected maneuver.

question: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches using lights and siren, what should you do?
options: a:Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection and wait.,c:Pull to the center and stop until it passes.
note: If an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and siren while you are already in an intersection, you should continue through the intersection if you can do so safely, then pull to the right side of the road and stop. Stopping in the middle of the intersection can block traffic and delay the emergency vehicle.

question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, what is the safest choice?
options: a:Avoid the puddle if possible.,b:Maintain the posted speed to drive through the water.,c:Shift into neutral as you drive through the water.
note: Deep puddles can cause hydroplaning, loss of steering control, or mechanical damage. If you can safely avoid a deep puddle by changing lanes or adjusting your path, that is the safest choice. If you must drive through water, slow down and proceed carefully, but you should never maintain high speed or rely on shifting to neutral as a safety measure.

question: In rainy weather you should be most cautious when turning or stopping:
options: a:One half hour after it stops raining.,b:After it has been raining all day.,c:During the first half hour of rain.
note: During the first 30 minutes or so of rain, oil and residue on the road surface mix with the water and make the pavement especially slippery. This is when you should be most cautious when turning or stopping, using lower speeds and greater following distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles arrive simultaneously from all directions, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Wait until there are no vehicles before proceeding.,b:The vehicle on your left.,c:The vehicle on your right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles arrive at the same time, drivers must yield to the vehicle on their right. This rule helps determine who goes first when there are no signs or signals. If you are unsure, it is always safer to yield and make eye contact with other drivers before proceeding.

question: When you see pedestrians near the roadway where you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain your speed.,b:Slow down and pass with caution.,c:Speed up to clear the area quickly.
note: When pedestrians are near the roadway, you must slow down, be prepared to stop, and pass with great caution. Pedestrians are vulnerable road users, and they may step into your path unexpectedly, so reducing speed and being ready to stop is the safest and legally expected behavior.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips along road edges or before intersections?
options: a:They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,b:They alert drivers to potential tire problems.,c:They vibrate and make noise to warn inattentive drivers they've left the travel lane.
note: Rumble strips are grooved or raised patterns on the road that cause noise and vibration when driven over. This alerts drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are drifting out of their lane or approaching a stop or hazard, giving them time to correct their path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If other drivers are passing you on both sides while you remain in the center expressway lane, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the lane on your right.,b:Stay in the center lane.,c:Move to the lane on your left.
note: On multi-lane roads, the right lane is generally for slower traffic and the left lane for passing. If vehicles are passing you on both sides while you are in the center lane, you are likely going slower than the flow of traffic. Safely moving to the right lane lets faster traffic pass and improves overall safety and traffic flow.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Turn up the radio to stay alert.,b:Find a safe place to stop and take a short nap.,c:Increase your speed to arrive sooner.
note: Driving while fatigued greatly increases your crash risk. If you feel drowsy, the safe action is to pull over at a safe place, such as a rest area or parking lot, and take a short nap or rest. Tricks like turning up the radio or speeding do not restore alertness and can be dangerous.

question: You are driving defensively when you:
options: a:Put one car length between you and the car ahead.,b:Only look at the car in front of you.,c:Keep your eyes moving to search for potential hazards.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road ahead, to the sides, and behind you so you can spot potential hazards early. By keeping your eyes moving instead of focusing only on the car in front, you have more time to react to sudden changes and avoid collisions.

question: You must use low beam headlights any time you are:
options: a:On a lighted street.,b:On a freeway.,c:In fog.
note: In fog and other low-visibility conditions, you should use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and reduce glare, improving your ability to see lane markings, other vehicles, and hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle under which of these conditions?
options: a:At a red traffic light and when a police officer orders you to stop.,b:Only where there is a red traffic light.,c:Only when a stop sign is present.
note: You must stop at red traffic lights and whenever a police officer directs you to stop, even if normal signals or signs would otherwise allow you to proceed. You are also required to stop at stop signs and in other situations (such as school buses with flashing red lights or at railroad crossings when required). Always obey both traffic control devices and lawful orders from officers.

question: What is the recommended placement of your hands to turn quickly and safely?
options: a:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,b:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.,c:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.
note: For quick, controlled steering, place your hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel, typically around the 9 and 3 o’clock positions. This gives you the best leverage and control for making smooth, precise turns and for quickly steering to avoid hazards while keeping the vehicle stable.

question: Holding a driver's license is considered a:
options: a:Requirement.,b:Privilege.,c:Right.
note: In the United States, driving is a privilege, not a right. The state grants you a driver’s license only if you meet certain requirements, and it can suspend or revoke that license if you drive unsafely, break traffic laws, or fail to meet legal obligations related to driving.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, you should use:
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: In rain, fog, snow, or sleet, use low beam headlights. Low beams help you see the road and make your vehicle more visible to others without causing glare. High beams can reflect off water droplets or fog and shine back into your eyes, reducing visibility. Parking lights alone are not sufficient for seeing or being seen.

question: When following a motorcycle, you should allow extra space in front of your vehicle because:
options: a:A station wagon stops more slowly.,b:A passenger vehicle requires more space.,c:Motorcycles can stop more quickly and are harder to see.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and can stop or swerve more quickly than larger vehicles, and they are harder to see in traffic. Leaving extra following distance gives you more time to notice their movements and react safely if they brake or need to avoid a hazard.

question: For drivers age 21 or older it is illegal to operate a vehicle with a BAC of at least:
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: Drivers 21 and older are legally impaired at a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher in Arkansas.

question: What is the first ability alcohol typically impairs?
options: a:Vision.,b:Judgment.,c:Balance.
note: Alcohol first affects the parts of the brain that control judgment and decision‑making. A driver may feel more confident and take more risks without realizing their abilities are reduced. As drinking continues, vision, balance, and coordination become more noticeably impaired.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers turning left must yield to:
options: a:Oncoming vehicles driving straight ahead.,b:No one; they have the right-of-way.,c:Only pedestrians, not vehicles.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, as well as to pedestrians in the crosswalk. You may only complete your left turn when there is a safe gap and no oncoming vehicles or pedestrians have the right‑of‑way.

question: Arkansas law requires drivers to turn on headlights when:
options: a:They are driving closely behind another vehicle.,b:When it is dark or visibility is reduced so you cannot see at least 500 feet ahead.,c:They want to get somebody's attention.
note: Arkansas law requires headlights to be on from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise and any time you cannot see clearly for at least 500 feet, such as in rain, snow, or fog. While it is a safe practice to use headlights when wipers are in use, the legal requirement is based on darkness and reduced visibility, not simply the use of windshield wipers.

question: Which factor influences how a person absorbs alcohol?
options: a:Height.,b:Intelligence.,c:Weight.
note: Alcohol affects people differently based on several physical factors. A person’s weight, sex, how much and how quickly they drink, and whether they have food in their stomach all influence how quickly alcohol is absorbed and how impaired they become. Mental traits like intelligence do not affect absorption. No matter what, only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol and become sober again.

question: Collisions are more likely to occur under which of these conditions?
options: a:Driving at the posted speed reduces risk.,b:One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.,c:All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.,d:One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.
note: Crashes are more likely when one vehicle is moving much faster or much slower than the surrounding traffic. Large speed differences force other drivers to brake, change lanes, or react suddenly, which increases the chance of a collision. When all vehicles travel at about the same safe speed, traffic flows more smoothly and predictably, reducing crash risk.

question: If conditions are very foggy, you should slow down and:
options: a:Use your low beam headlights.,b:Turn on your emergency flashers.,c:Use your high beam headlights.
note: In fog, you should slow down and use low beam headlights. Low beams and fog lights (if your vehicle has them) aim light down toward the road and reduce glare. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Emergency flashers are for stopped or very slow-moving vehicles, not normal driving in fog.

question: How far down the road should you look to avoid last-minute braking or turning?
options: a:About 15 seconds ahead.,b:About 3 seconds ahead.,c:About 10 seconds ahead.
note: Good drivers look well ahead so they can see problems early and avoid sudden braking or swerving. A common safe-driving rule is to scan the road about 10 seconds ahead of your vehicle. Looking this far ahead gives you time to notice hazards, adjust your speed, and change lanes smoothly, which helps prevent last‑minute maneuvers that can cause crashes.

question: Reaction time is likely to be slower after:
options: a:Drinking alcohol.,b:Sleeping.,c:Working hard.
note: Alcohol slows the brain and nervous system, which delays how quickly you can see a hazard, decide what to do, and move your hands or feet to react. This slower reaction time makes it harder to avoid sudden dangers on the road. Even small amounts of alcohol can affect reaction time and judgment, so you should never drive after drinking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your original lane after passing another vehicle, what should you see?
options: a:Both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:Beep your horn to signal your move.,c:Flash your headlights.
note: Before moving back into your original lane after passing, you should not rely on guesswork or just feeling clear of the other vehicle. Wait until you can clearly see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your inside rearview mirror. This shows you have enough space ahead of that vehicle so you can return to the lane without cutting them off or forcing them to brake.

question: A dashed white line down the center of a roadway indicates what?
options: a:Lanes travel in opposite directions and drivers may pass.,b:Lanes travel in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,c:Lanes travel in the same direction and drivers may pass when safe.
note: A dashed white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. Drivers may change lanes or pass another vehicle when it is safe and legal to do so. White lines never separate traffic moving in opposite directions; that is done with yellow lines.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When facing a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection, you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the pedestrians.,b:Proceed because you have the green light.,c:Wait until vehicles have cleared before yielding to pedestrians.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the intersection even when facing a green signal, especially when turning.

question: If bad weather reduces your visibility, you should:
options: a:Drive faster to get off the road quicker.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
note: When bad weather reduces visibility, you should slow down and increase your following distance. More space gives you extra time to see hazards and react if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. Driving faster or closer to oncoming traffic increases the risk of a collision in low-visibility conditions.

question: What is the definition of a crosswalk?
options: a:Another name for a four-way intersection.,b:An area reserved for road construction workers.,c:The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.
note: A crosswalk is the part of the roadway set aside for pedestrians to cross. It can be marked with painted lines or be an unmarked extension of the sidewalk across the street at an intersection. Drivers must watch for pedestrians in crosswalks and yield to them as required by law.

question: When driving through a work zone, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop suddenly.,b:Increase your speed to clear the zone quickly.,c:Maintain your normal speed throughout the zone.
note: In work zones you must slow down, obey all posted work-zone signs, and be ready to stop suddenly for workers, equipment, or lane shifts. Higher speeds greatly increase the risk of crashes in these changing conditions.

question: If you have a sudden tire blowout while driving, you should:
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly.,b:Pump the brakes.,c:Use the brakes lightly and slow gradually.
note: With a tire blowout, grip the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow while you brake gently if needed. Hard or sudden braking can cause loss of control, especially at higher speeds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic light should be treated as:
options: a:An indicator you are traveling the wrong way.,b:A stop sign (come to a complete stop),c:A signal you may not proceed until it turns green.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, then proceed only when it is safe and after yielding to pedestrians and other traffic, just as you would at a stop sign.

question: What does a solid white center line mean on a roadway with lanes in the same direction?
options: a:Lanes travel in the same direction and lane changes are discouraged and should generally not be made.,b:Lanes travel in opposite directions and drivers may pass.,c:Lanes travel in the same direction and lane changes are allowed when the line is broken.
note: A solid white line between lanes going in the same direction means lane changes are discouraged and should generally not be made, except when necessary and safe. These lines are used where lane changes can be especially risky, such as near intersections or freeway exits.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:You may pass on the right when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:You may pass on the left when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and allows passing on the left when there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe. You must return to your lane before coming within a safe distance of oncoming vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle on its left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After about three seconds have passed.,c:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: After you pass, you should not move back into the right lane until you can clearly see the front of the vehicle you passed in your inside rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space ahead of that vehicle so you can return without cutting them off or forcing them to brake.

question: Which statement about backing your vehicle is true?
options: a:Backing up is only dangerous in large vehicles.,b:Backing up is always potentially dangerous.,c:Backing up is dangerous only without a helper.
note: Backing is always potentially dangerous because your view to the rear and sides is limited and it is harder to see small children, pedestrians, or obstacles. Always back slowly, check mirrors and over your shoulder, and use a helper when possible to reduce the risk of a collision.

question: If you've had several beers, the only way to reduce alcohol's effects is to:
options: a:Take a cold shower.,b:Wait several hours.,c:Drink several cups of coffee.
note: Only time reduces the effects of alcohol. Your body eliminates alcohol at a fairly steady rate, roughly about one drink per hour. Cold showers, coffee, or exercise may make you feel more awake, but they do not lower your blood alcohol concentration or make you safe to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic should yield to you.,c:You never have to yield when turning left.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians who are in or entering the crosswalk you will cross. Do not start your turn until you are sure oncoming traffic and pedestrians have cleared and it is safe to complete the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting the freeway onto a ramp that curves downhill, you should:
options: a:Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.,b:Slow to a safe speed before the curve.,c:Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
note: When exiting onto a downhill, curving ramp, you should slow to a safe speed before you enter the curve. Braking hard while already in the curve can cause skidding or loss of control, especially on a downgrade. Use the advisory speed on the ramp sign as a guide and adjust for traffic and conditions.

question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, you may:
options: a:Cross the centerline to change lanes when safe.,b:Must stay strictly within your lane.,c:Change lanes only from the left lane.
note: A single broken white centerline separates lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so. You must still check mirrors, signal, and yield to vehicles already in the lane you are entering.

question: In which situation should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,b:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,c:When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.
note: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light, you should keep your wheels pointed straight ahead. If your wheels are turned and you are hit from behind, your vehicle can be pushed into oncoming traffic. When parked on a hill or on a level road with no curb, you should turn your wheels so that if the vehicle rolls, it moves away from traffic, not into it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking, your vehicle should be parked within how many inches of the curb?
options: a:Six inches.,b:Twelve inches.,c:Eighteen inches.
note: When parallel parking, your vehicle should be close enough to the curb to be out of moving traffic but not so far that it creates a hazard. Many states, including Arkansas, require you to be no more than 18 inches from the curb. Always check your state’s handbook for the exact distance, but 18 inches is a common legal maximum.

question: How are fines for moving traffic violations in work zones typically handled in Arkansas?
options: a:Lessened.,b:Doubled.,c:Non-existent.
note: In Arkansas, fines for moving traffic violations in work zones are typically doubled when workers are present and proper warning signs are posted. This is to encourage drivers to slow down and use extra caution to protect road workers.

question: Which road surface is most likely to freeze first?
options: a:A tunnel,b:A bridge,c:An intersection
note: Bridges and overpasses usually freeze before the rest of the roadway because they are exposed to cold air from above and below. This causes ice to form sooner and remain longer than on regular road surfaces, even if the nearby pavement looks clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When the driver you passed signals for you to return to your lane.,c:When you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After you pass, you need enough space before returning to the right lane. A good rule is to wait until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed, including its headlights, in your inside rearview mirror. That means you have cleared the vehicle and can move back without cutting it off.

question: If the rear of your vehicle is sliding left, how should you steer?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel left (in the direction of the skid).,b:Do not turn the steering wheel.,c:Turn the steering wheel right (opposite the skid).
note: In a rear-wheel skid, always steer in the direction the rear of your vehicle is sliding. If the rear slides left, you turn the steering wheel left. This helps the vehicle straighten out and regain traction. At the same time, ease off the accelerator and avoid hard braking, which can make the skid worse.

question: If a vehicle is equipped with airbags, you should:
options: a:Wear seat belts behind your back for added protection.,b:Still wear seat belts.,c:Not wear seat belts because airbags are enough.
note: Airbags are designed to work together with seat belts, not replace them. You must still wear your lap and shoulder belt even if your vehicle has airbags. Seat belts keep you properly positioned so the airbag can protect you effectively and reduce the risk of serious injury.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors while driving?
options: a:Only when it is absolutely necessary.,b:Often, to know how traffic is moving behind you.,c:Only when you are slowing down.
note: You should check your mirrors frequently—about every few seconds—to stay aware of traffic behind and beside you. Regular mirror checks help you spot fast-approaching vehicles, tailgaters, and vehicles in adjacent lanes so you can change lanes, slow, or stop more safely.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving, what is the correct action?
options: a:Signal and move into the slow lane.,b:Put on your hazard lights and pull safely off the road.,c:Stop in your lane and turn on your hazard lights.
note: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem, signal, move off the roadway to the right shoulder or a safe area if possible, and then turn on your hazard lights. Getting out of the traffic lane greatly reduces the risk of being hit, and the flashing lights warn other drivers that your vehicle is disabled.

question: Which of these is a sign of an aggressive driver?
options: a:Erratic and improper lane changes.,b:Having many passengers in the car.,c:Driving slowly.
note: Erratic, improper lane changes are a classic sign of aggressive driving. Aggressive drivers weave through traffic, change lanes without signaling, and make sudden, unsafe moves. You should not engage with them; instead, create space and let them go ahead.

question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead,b:Right, toward the side of the road.,c:Left, toward the center of the road.
note: On a two-way road with no curb, you always turn your front wheels so that if the vehicle rolls, it will move away from traffic and off the roadway. Pointing the wheels right, toward the side of the road, ensures the car will roll toward the shoulder if the brakes fail.

question: What is a major consequence of excessive speed?
options: a:It increases the likelihood of serious injury and death.,b:It helps you maneuver around obstacles better.,c:Saves significant travel time.
note: Excessive speed greatly increases both the chance of a crash and how severe the injuries will be. At higher speeds you have less time to react, need more distance to stop, and crashes involve more force, leading to more serious injuries and deaths.

question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Construction workers must yield to vehicles.,b:Pedestrians must yield to vehicles.,c:Pedestrians must be yielded to by vehicles.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks. When a pedestrian is in a marked or unmarked crosswalk at an intersection, you must slow or stop to let them cross, unless a traffic signal or officer clearly gives them a red or "don’t walk" indication and they are not yet in the crosswalk.

question: If there is no marked crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, you must:
options: a:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,b:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if no crosswalk is marked; stop and allow them to cross safely.

question: As your speed increases, what becomes especially important?
options: a:Turning on your headlights.,b:Looking well ahead of your vehicle.,c:Changing lanes frequently.
note: As speed increases, you need more time and distance to react and stop. Looking well ahead lets you spot hazards early, adjust speed smoothly, and avoid sudden braking or swerving.

question: A responsible driver should:
options: a:Stare directly in front of the car.,b:Only focus on the middle of the road.,c:Watch beside, ahead, and to the rear of the vehicle.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan in all directions—ahead, to the sides, and behind—so they can see hazards early, check blind spots, and respond safely to changing traffic conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Within a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles.,b:Within an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles.,c:Where signs and pavement markings permit passing.
note: Passing is only safe and legal where signs and pavement markings allow it and when you have enough clear space to complete the pass without interfering with oncoming traffic or the vehicle you are passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, which statement is correct regarding yielding?
options: a:You must always yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.,c:You should never yield.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Turn only when the way is clear and it is safe to complete the turn.

question: Where is the safest place for children age 12 and under in a vehicle with airbags?
options: a:The back seat.,b:The front seat.,c:The bed of a pickup truck.
note: Children 12 and under are safest in the back seat, properly restrained. Front airbags deploy with great force and are designed for adults, so young children should ride in the rear seats whenever possible.

question: How can you help keep the driver behind you a safe distance away?
options: a:Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.,b:Maintain a steady speed and signal your intentions early.,c:Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
note: Maintaining a steady speed and signaling early makes your driving predictable. When the driver behind you can anticipate your actions, they are more likely to leave a safe following distance and avoid sudden braking or tailgating.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, you should:
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down passing cars.,b:Sound your horn to get attention.,c:Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if safe to do so.
note: On high‑speed roads, you should pull completely onto the shoulder if possible, turn on your hazard flashers so others see you, and stay inside the vehicle with your seat belt on unless there is an immediate danger such as fire. Standing outside near fast traffic is very dangerous.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is correct?
options: a:If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it's safe to drive.,b:Alcohol impairs judgment, which is essential for safe driving.,c:If you are under the legal BAC limit, your driving is not impaired.
note: Alcohol reduces judgment, coordination, and reaction time, even at low levels. You can be unsafe to drive even if you feel fine or are under the legal BAC limit, so you should never rely on how you feel or simple tests like walking a straight line.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which passing actions are unlawful?
options: a:Passing in a marked no passing zone or passing over a railroad crossing.,b:Passing only on the left when safe.,c:Passing on a road with a broken yellow centerline to your side.
note: Passing is illegal and unsafe in marked no‑passing zones, at or near railroad crossings, and in other areas where visibility is limited, such as hills and curves. You should only pass where it is both legal and clearly safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is required for safe interstate driving?
options: a:Both the ability to drive safely at higher speeds and constant alertness.,b:The ability to drive at increased speeds only.,c:Constant alertness only.
note: Interstate driving involves higher speeds and heavier traffic, so you must be able to control your vehicle smoothly at those speeds and stay constantly alert to changing conditions, signs, and other road users.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, you should:
options: a:Follow closely because the trucker can see farther ahead.,b:Stay no more than one car length behind.,c:Follow farther behind than you would a passenger vehicle.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots and need more distance to stop. By following farther behind than you would a passenger vehicle, you stay out of the truck’s blind spots and give yourself more time and space to react if traffic slows or stops.

question: When bicycles are used on roadways, they are considered:
options: a:Vehicles.,b:Hazards.,c:Dangerous obstacles.
note: On public roads, bicycles are treated as vehicles. Bicyclists must obey traffic signals, signs, and lane markings, and drivers must yield, signal, and share the road with them just as they do with other vehicles.

question: With oncoming vehicles to your left and parked vehicles to your right, how should you steer?
options: a:Take a middle course between the oncoming traffic and the parked cars.,b:Steer closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.,c:Steer closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming traffic.
note: When you have oncoming traffic on the left and parked cars on the right, keep your vehicle centered in your lane. This middle position gives you the most clearance from both hazards and reduces the chance of sideswiping a parked car or drifting toward oncoming traffic.

question: An orange and red triangular emblem displayed on the back of a vehicle indicates:
options: a:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:A slow-moving vehicle.,c:Shoulder work ahead.
note: An orange and red triangular emblem on the back of a vehicle means it is a slow‑moving vehicle, such as farm equipment or certain maintenance vehicles. When you see this emblem, be prepared to slow down and pass only when it is safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, what assumption should you avoid making?
options: a:That the other driver will make space for you to return to the lane.,b:That the other driver won't move.,c:That you can pass regardless of visibility.
note: When passing, you must never assume other drivers will slow down or leave space for you to return. Before you move out to pass, make sure you have enough clear distance ahead and a safe gap to move back into your lane without relying on the other driver to adjust.

question: Which behavior tends to block the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.,b:Slowing down to look at a collision scene.,c:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
note: Slowing down just to look at a crash or anything unusual on the road is called rubbernecking. It distracts you, makes you unpredictable, and causes traffic to back up. Using public transportation or avoiding unnecessary lane changes does not block traffic flow; rubbernecking does.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Pull over quickly.,b:Apply the brake and hold it.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly and brake lightly.
note: When a tire blows out, the key is to stay in control. Grip the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and brake gently once the vehicle is stable. Sudden hard braking or jerking the wheel can cause you to lose control. After slowing, move off the road when it is safe.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true (repeat)?
options: a:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,b:Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror.,c:Blind spots can be seen in your rearview mirror.
note: All vehicles have blind spots, but large trucks have much larger blind areas on all sides than passenger cars. Even with properly adjusted mirrors, you cannot see everything, so you should avoid driving alongside or close behind large trucks where the driver may not see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To safely enter a gap in highway traffic you should:
options: a:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.,b:Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.,c:Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.
note: To enter a gap in highway traffic safely, you must know what is happening both behind and ahead. First check behind you to be sure it is safe to adjust your speed or change lanes, then watch the traffic in front to judge the size of the gap and merge smoothly without forcing others to brake hard.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:
options: a:Be ready to drive faster than the train.,b:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.,c:Look for a way around lowered gates.
note: A railroad crossing warning sign means you are approaching tracks and must be ready to stop if a train is coming. Slow down, look and listen for trains, and obey all signals and gates. Never try to beat a train or drive around lowered gates, as trains cannot stop quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you enter a roundabout, what must you do?
options: a:Yield only to cars already in the roundabout.,b:Yield only to pedestrians.,c:Yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and any traffic already in the roundabout.
note: When approaching a roundabout, you must yield to anyone already using it. That includes pedestrians in crosswalks, bicyclists, and vehicles already circulating in the roundabout. Enter only when there is a safe gap so you do not force others to brake or swerve.

question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain/snow, a good way to make sure other drivers see you is to:
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Turn up the instrument panel lights.,c:Use parking lights only.
note: In low‑light or reduced‑visibility conditions such as dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, you should turn on your low‑beam headlights. Headlights make your vehicle easier for others to see and also improve your own view of the road. Parking lights alone are not sufficient and are often illegal to use while moving.

question: If you park where vehicles don't normally park, what must you ensure?
options: a:That your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,b:That your reverse lights remain on.,c:That you park five feet from the curb.
note: If you must park in an unusual place where vehicles do not normally park, you must make sure your vehicle can be clearly seen by drivers approaching from any direction. Good visibility helps prevent other drivers from being surprised and reduces the chance of a collision with your parked vehicle.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered distracting?
options: a:Because it occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind and diverts attention from driving.,b:Because it makes the driver worry about call costs.,c:Because it distracts other drivers.
note: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it takes your attention away from driving. Your hands may be off the wheel, your eyes may leave the road, and your mind is focused on the conversation instead of traffic. Even hands‑free use can mentally distract you and increase crash risk.

question: Before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign, what should you do first?
options: a:Set the parking brake.,b:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,c:Press down hard on the accelerator.
note: Before you slow or stop for a signal or sign, check your mirrors so you know what traffic is doing behind and around you. This helps you brake smoothly and early, giving drivers behind you time to react and reducing the risk of being hit from the rear.

question: When a school bus is stopped ahead on your side of the road with red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the bus's red lights stop flashing.,b:Slow to 10 mph and proceed cautiously.,c:Change lanes and pass cautiously.
note: When a school bus has activated red flashing lights and its stop arm, traffic in both directions must stop until the lights are turned off and the arm is retracted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To check blind spots when changing lanes, a driver should look:
options: a:Only at the left outside mirror.,b:Over their left or right shoulder.,c:Only at the inside rearview mirror.
note: To check blind spots before changing lanes, quickly glance over the shoulder on the side you are moving toward. Mirrors do not show the entire area around your vehicle, so a shoulder check helps you see vehicles, motorcycles, bicycles, or pedestrians that may be hidden in your blind spots.

question: Before turning the ignition in a vehicle, what should you do regarding seat belts?
options: a:Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts and buckle your own.,b:Buckle your safety belt but not worry about passengers.,c:Start the engine and then advise passengers to buckle up.
note: Before starting the engine, the driver should buckle their own seat belt and make sure all passengers are properly buckled. Making this a routine helps ensure everyone is protected in case of a sudden stop or crash.

question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, how should you drive relative to your headlights?
options: a:Slow enough so you can stop within the distance illuminated by your headlights.,b:Use high beams all the time to see better.,c:Keep instrument panel lights bright so others can see you.
note: At night, you must drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance you can see with your headlights. This is called not overdriving your headlights. If you go faster than this, you may not have enough distance to see and react to hazards in time.

question: Before entering an intersection, where should you look?
options: a:Only to the right.,b:Left, then right, then left again.,c:Only to the left.
note: Before entering an intersection, look left, then right, then left again. Traffic closest to you usually comes from the left, so checking that direction twice helps you spot any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians that may be approaching.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do about braking?
options: a:Pump the brakes continuously.,b:Stay off the brakes until you regain control.,c:Apply the brakes firmly immediately.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, take your foot off the accelerator and avoid braking until you regain control of the vehicle. Braking can lock the wheels and make the skid worse. If your vehicle has ABS and you must brake to avoid a collision, press the brake pedal firmly and steadily while steering in the direction you want the front of the car to go.

question: How should you apply the gas pedal for safe control?
options: a:As quickly as possible.,b:Slowly and smoothly.,c:By lightly tapping.
note: Press the gas pedal slowly and smoothly so you can accelerate under control. Gentle pressure helps prevent wheel spin, sudden surges of speed, and loss of traction, especially on wet, icy, or gravel surfaces.

question: If conditions require you to have lights on, which should you use?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:High beams.,c:Low beams.
note: When conditions require you to have your lights on—such as rain, fog, snow, or reduced visibility—you should use low beam headlights. High beams can reflect off fog, rain, or snow and create glare, making it harder to see.

question: When should you fasten your safety belt?
options: a:Before the engine is started.,b:Whenever you feel unsafe.,c:After reaching speeds over 45 mph.
note: Seat belts should be fastened before starting the engine; in most jurisdictions belt use is required by law.

question: What helps prevent you from becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Tailgate the driver ahead of you.,b:Drive above the posted speed limit to get ahead.,c:Relax, concentrate on driving, and be realistic about travel time.
note: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, stay calm, focus on safe driving, and allow realistic travel time so you are not rushed. Do not take other drivers’ mistakes personally, and obey speed limits and following distances to reduce stress and conflict on the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?
options: a:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,b:Change lanes while driving through an intersection.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: You should not change lanes while you are in the middle of an intersection. Lane changes should be completed before you enter or after you exit the intersection, and you must always check mirrors and blind spots and ensure it is safe before moving into another lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection where the signal has just turned steady yellow and you have not entered yet, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a safe stop before the intersection.,b:Speed up to beat the light.,c:Reduce speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection and can stop safely, you must slow down and stop before the intersection, rather than speeding up to beat the light.

question: Which best describes how defensive drivers think?
options: a:They consider what other drivers might do and prepare to react.,b:They assume other drivers will always do the right thing.,c:They expect no breaks or courtesy from other drivers.
note: Defensive drivers constantly scan the road and think ahead about what other drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists might do. They prepare to react safely to mistakes by others by adjusting speed, following distance, and lane position to reduce crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at a corner, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right, and pedestrians and bicyclists in the crosswalk.,b:Pedestrians waiting with a "Walk" signal.,c:Oncoming vehicles also turning left.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, and to pedestrians and bicyclists in the crosswalk. You do not automatically yield to every approaching vehicle regardless of its signal, but you must yield to any traffic that has the right-of-way and would be affected by your turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, what should you do?
options: a:Stop well behind the gates and wait until they are lifted and the tracks are clear.,b:Slow down and drive around the gates if you do not see a train.,c:Drive around the crossing gates if you can't see a train.
note: When gates are down and lights are flashing at a railroad crossing, you must stop at a safe distance behind the gates and wait. Never drive around or under lowered gates, even if you do not see a train, and proceed only after the gates are fully raised and the tracks are clear.

question: If your vehicle has ABS and you're stopping on snow or ice, you should:
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,b:Pump the brakes manually.,c:Avoid using the brakes and let the car roll to a stop.
note: With ABS, you should press the brake pedal firmly and keep holding it. The ABS system automatically pumps the brakes to prevent wheel lockup and help you maintain steering control, especially on slippery surfaces like snow or ice.

question: Which of the following statements about work zones is correct?
options: a:Fines are the same as under normal conditions.,b:You must "Slow for the Cone Zone.",c:Only slow down if you think workers are present.
note: Work zones require you to slow down and drive with extra caution, whether or not you see workers present. Many states increase fines in work zones and use phrases like “Slow for the Cone Zone” to remind drivers to reduce speed and be alert.

question: Any amount of alcohol in a driver's blood can impair what?
options: a:Judgment and physical coordination.,b:Right-of-way privileges.,c:Knowledge only.
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect your judgment, reaction time, and coordination. Even if you are below the legal limit, your ability to make safe driving decisions and control the vehicle can be impaired.

question: In foggy conditions, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Use your high beam headlights.,b:Use your parking lights.,c:Use your low beam headlights.
note: In fog, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back at you, making it harder to see. Low beams and, if equipped, fog lights help you see the road and be seen by others.

question: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:
options: a:There isn't room on the other side for you to completely cross the tracks.,b:The railroad crossing is located in a city or town with frequent train traffic.,c:You are transporting two or more young children.
note: You must never stop on railroad tracks. If there is not enough room on the far side for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks, wait before the tracks until you are sure you can cross all the way without stopping.

question: At intersections, crosswalks, or railroad crossings you should always do what to check for hazards?
options: a:Never pass vehicles that are stopped at a crosswalk or intersection without knowing why they are stopped.,b:Stop completely at all intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings.,c:Look to the sides of your vehicle (left and right) to see what is coming.
note: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you must scan for hazards by looking to both sides of your vehicle (left and right) to see if pedestrians, cyclists, or other vehicles are approaching. Never pass vehicles that are stopped at a crosswalk or intersection without knowing why they are stopped, because they may be yielding to someone you cannot see.

question: Where are a truck's blind spots typically located?
options: a:On both sides of the truck and directly behind the truck.,b:Directly behind the cab only.,c:On the immediate left of the cab only.
note: Large trucks have large blind spots, often called "no-zones," along both sides of the truck and directly behind it. If you cannot see the truck driver in the truck’s side mirrors, the driver probably cannot see you. Avoid lingering in these areas, especially close behind the truck or along the immediate left or right of the cab and trailer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, you may turn left onto another one-way street only if:
options: a:You increase your speed before the turn.,b:Traffic on the street moves to the right.,c:Traffic on the street moves to the left.
